question: What are the primary stages of the High Pressure Compressor (HPC) from which engine air is bled?

options.a: Low Pressure (LP) and Intermediate Pressure (IP) stages
options.b: Intermediate Pressure (IP) and High Pressure (HP) stages
options.c: Fan discharge air and HP stages

justification: According to the Engine Bleed description, air is bled from two engine High Pressure Compressor (HPC) stages: the Intermediate Pressure (IP) stage and the HP stage.

question: Which component acts as the main shut-off and overall system pressure regulating valve for engine bleed air?

options.b: The Overpressure Valve (OPV)
options.c: The Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV)

justification: The training manual states all engine bleed air is supplied through the main engine bleed valve, also known as the Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV), which acts as a shut off and overall system pressure regulating valve.

question: How is the switching between the IP and HP bleed stages achieved during engine operation?

options.a: Electrically by the Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC) based on altitude
options.b: Pneumatically when the IP stage pressure is insufficient at low engine speeds
options.c: Hydraulically through the engine interface unit

justification: The manual states switching between IP and HP is done pneumatically when the IP stage pressure is not sufficient (engine at low speed).

question: What is the function of the Fan Air Valve (FAV) within the engine bleed system?

options.a: It regulates the airflow from the HP stage into the PRV
options.b: It modulates fan discharge air across the precooler to maintain temperature within limits
options.c: It provides backup pressure regulation if the PRV fails

justification: The temperature of engine bleed air is regulated using a precooler; fan discharge air is modulated by the Fan Air Valve (FAV) to blow across the precooler and maintain temperature within limits.

question: What regulates the bleed air pressure when it is supplied by the HP stage of the engine?

options.b: The High Pressure Valve (HPV)
options.c: The Precooler Thermostat

justification: The engine air bleed pressure is pneumatically regulated by the High Pressure Valve (VLV) when air is supplied by the HP stage.

question: At what specific temperature will a thermal fuse cause the Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV) to close in the event of an engine fire?
justification: The Engine Bleed System Description states that a thermal fuse causes the PRV to close in case of engine fire at 450°C (842°F).

question: In what conditions will the Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC) automatically energize the control solenoid to shut off the PRV?

options.a: When the Fan Air Valve (FAV) reaches its maximum open position
options.b: When downstream temperature of the precooler exceeds 257°C (527°F)
options.c: When engine power increases above the takeoff threshold

justification: The solenoid is automatically energized by the BMC to shut off the PRV in cases of over-temperature downstream of the precooler (above 257°C).

question: At what pressure does the Overpressure Valve (OPV) become fully closed to protect the system?

options.b: 75 psi
options.c: 85 psi

justification: The OPV starts to close at 75 psi and is fully closed at 85 psi.

question: If the High Pressure Valve (HPV) fails, what is the mandatory deactivation position required for dispatch per the MEL?

options.b: CLOSED
options.c: AUTO

justification: In case of failure, the pneumatic system HPV must be deactivated CLOSED for dispatch per the Minimum Equipment List.

question: What is the procedure for manually deactivating the Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV) into the CLOSED position?

options.a: Move the manual override to the CLOSED position and secure with a locking pin
options.b: Disconnect the electrical solenoid and cap the pneumatic sense line
options.c: Rotate the internal butterfly valve 90 degrees using a standard hex key

justification: The deactivation procedure requires moving the manual override to the CLOSED position and securing it with a locking pin.

question: How many leak detection loops monitor the hot air supply ducts in the pneumatic system?

options.b: Three loops: Pylon, Wing, and APU
options.c: Four loops: Engine 1, Engine 2, APU, and Ground

justification: The leak detection system is organized into three loops: PYLON, WING, and APU.

question: Which computer system is responsible for receiving signals from the leak detection loops and triggering warnings?

options.b: The Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC)
options.c: The Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC)

justification: Leak detection loops are installed along the ducts and are connected to the BMCs.

question: Which areas are specifically monitored by the WING leak detection loop on the A320 family?

options.b: Wing leading edge, air conditioning compartment (belly fairing), and APU forward supply duct
options.c: Wing slats, engine pylons, and center tank area

justification: The WING detection elements monitor the wing leading edge, air conditioning compartment (belly fairing), and APU forward supply duct.

question: What is the sensor arrangement for the WING leak detection system to ensure reliable overheat detection?

options.a: A single loop system with redundant sensors
options.b: A dual-loop system where both loops A and B must detect an overheat to trigger a warning
options.c: Independent sensors connected in parallel with individual cockpit indicators

justification: WING leak detection is a dual-loop system. To generate a WING LEAK warning, both A and B loops have to detect the overheat.

question: How do the BMCs handle wing double loop detection signals?

options.a: They process signals independently without data exchange
options.b: They exchange data via an ARINC bus to activate warnings through an AND logic
options.c: They use a Master/Slave configuration where BMC 1 performs all logic

justification: Both BMCs receive signals from the loops and exchange data via an ARINC bus for the wing double loop detection to allow warnings to be activated through an AND logic.

question: If a single WING loop fails, what maintenance message is displayed on the ECAM STATUS page?

options.b: AIR BLEED
options.c: BMC FAULT

justification: If a single loop fails, the MAINTENANCE message AIR BLEED will be displayed on the STATUS page associated with a CFDS message L(R) WING LOOP (INOP).

question: What is the consequence of a BMC 1 failure regarding the APU BLEED LEAK warning?

options.a: BMC 2 takes over and triggers the warning automatically
options.b: The APU BLEED LEAK warning is lost
options.c: The APU Bleed valve closes automatically to prevent potential damage

justification: The manual states the APU BLEED LEAK warning is lost if BMC 1 is failed because the APU loop is connected to BMC 1 only.

question: Which valves are automatically commanded to close if an Engine 1 pylon or LH wing leak is detected?

options.a: PRV 1, Anti-ice valve 1, and APU Bleed valve
options.b: PRV 1, X-Bleed valve (in AUTO), and PRV 2
options.c: PRV 1, Anti-ice valve 1, X-Bleed valve (in AUTO), and APU Bleed valve

justification: The Leak Consequence table shows that an ENG 1 FAULT (Pylon or LH Wing Leak) causes closure of PRV 1, Anti-ice valve 1, X-Bleed valve (in Auto), and APU Bleed valve.

question: Do the APU and crossbleed (X-BLEED) valves close automatically during a Main Engine Start (MES) if a leak is detected?

options.a: Yes, to prevent hot air exposure to the starting engine
options.b: No, they do not close during Main Engine Start
options.c: Only if both BMCs detect the leak simultaneously

justification: The manual includes a specific note: APU and cross bleed (X-BLEED) valves do not close during Main Engine Start (MES).

question: What is required for dispatch if a WING leak detection loop fails?

options.a: Both loops on that wing must be replaced immediately
options.b: At least one loop on each wing must be operational
options.c: The aircraft cannot be dispatched into known icing conditions

justification: The manual states for dispatch, WING leak detection must be operational (at least one loop) on each wing.

question: To which side of the crossbleed duct is the APU bleed supply connected?

options.b: Left side
options.c: Center manifold

justification: The APU bleed supply is connected to the left side of the crossbleed duct.

question: Where is the crossbleed valve located on the aircraft?

options.b: In the forward section of the lower fuselage belly fairing area
options.c: In the aft fuselage near the APU firewall

justification: The crossbleed valve is in the forward section of the lower fuselage belly fairing area.

question: What occurs when the APU BLEED P/BSW is selected ON while the X-BLEED valve is in the AUTO position?

options.a: The APU bleed valve opens and the X-BLEED valve stays closed
options.b: The APU bleed valve opens, the PRVs are maintained closed, and the X-BLEED valve opens automatically
options.c: The engine PRVs open to augment the APU air supply

justification: When APU BLEED is ON, the APU bleed valve opens, the PRVs are maintained electrically closed and the X-BLEED valve is automatically opened (if in AUTO).

question: What type of electrical motors operate the crossbleed (X-BLEED) valve?

options.b: One stepper motor for precision control
options.c: Two electrical DC motors

justification: The crossbleed (X-BLEED) valve is an electrically controlled shut-off valve operated by two electrical DC motors.

question: How do the APU bleed valves for the Garrett and Honeywell APUs operate in the absence of air pressure or electrical power?

options.a: They fail in the last commanded position
options.b: They are spring-loaded closed
options.c: They are spring-loaded open to ensure engine starting capability

justification: For the Garrett and Honeywell APUs, in the absence of air pressure or electrical power, the valves are spring-loaded closed.

question: Which cockpit control position is used to confirm the automatic closure of the X-BLEED valve during a leak detection test?

options.b: AUTO
options.c: SHUT

justification: The SHUT position of the X-BLEED selector is used to confirm automatic closure during bleed leak detection.

question: When using a ground air supply, how can the right-hand (RH) pneumatic system be supplied?

options.b: By opening the crossbleed valve
options.c: Through a second HP ground connector on the RH side

justification: On the ground, an HP ground power unit can be connected to the left side; the right side may be supplied by opening the crossbleed valve.

question: What is the recommended sequence for an engine start using ground air for maximum safety?

options.a: Start both engines simultaneously while connected to the ground cart
options.b: Start the first engine, disconnect the ground air supply, and perform a crossbleed start for the second engine
options.c: Start the second engine first to check the RH system integrity

justification: For safety, it is recommended to use the ground air supply to start the first engine, then disconnect and perform a crossbleed start for the second engine.

question: Does the 'GND' indication on the ECAM BLEED page confirm that a ground air supply is connected?

options.a: Yes, it is triggered by a pressure switch in the ground supply duct
options.b: No, it only indicates the aircraft is on the ground and shows the supply point is on the left side
options.c: Only if the X-BLEED valve is in the OPEN position

justification: The GND indication DOES NOT indicate ground air supply connected or available. It appears when the aircraft is on the ground to show that ground air is directly supplied to the LEFT side only.

question: What is the function of the secondary motor in the X-BLEED valve assembly?

options.a: It provides backup for the automatic mode if the primary fails
options.b: It is used for manual operation via the overhead panel selector
options.c: It drives the valve to the closed position during engine fire conditions

justification: The X-BLEED valve is operated by two electrical DC motors: the primary is for AUTO mode, and the secondary motor is used for manual operation controlled by the selector on the overhead panel.

question: Where are the two air conditioning packs located on the Airbus Single Aisle family?

options.a: In the aft fuselage area near the APU
options.b: In the wing root area, forward of the landing gear bay
options.c: Under the cockpit floor

justification: The packs are installed in the wing root area, forward of the landing gear bay in the air conditioning bay.

question: What is the function of the mixer unit in the air conditioning system?

options.a: It mixes hot trim air with the bleed air before it enters the pack
options.b: It mixes air from the packs with re-circulated air from the cabin
options.c: It combines the flow from both engines to provide a single supply to the cockpit

justification: The packs supply air to the mixer unit, which mixes air from the packs and re-circulated air from the cabin before distribution.

question: Which component is primarily responsible for calculating flow mass demand and positioning the pack Flow Control Valve (FCV)?

options.b: The Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC)
options.c: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU)

justification: During normal operation, the Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC) calculates the flow mass demand and sets the FCV in the necessary reference position.

question: Why are two cabin recirculation fans installed in the air conditioning system?

options.a: To provide backup cooling if the packs fail
options.b: To reduce bleed air demand and save fuel
options.c: To ensure positive pressure in the cargo compartments

justification: Two cabin recirculation fans are installed to reduce the bleed air demand and therefore save fuel.

question: By what means does the ACSC control the air conditioning pack outlet temperature?

options.a: By modulating the bypass valve and the ram air inlet doors
options.b: By varying the speed of the Air Cycle Machine
options.c: By adjusting the pressure of the trim air system

justification: To control the pack outlet temperature, the ACSC modulates the BYPASS VALVE and the RAM AIR INLET doors.

question: What is the consequence of the pack compressor outlet temperature exceeding 215°C (419°F)?

options.a: The pack overheat warning is immediately triggered
options.b: The Flow Control Valve (FCV) starts to reduce the flow
options.c: The bypass valve is driven fully open to protect the turbine

justification: If the pack compressor outlet temperature is > 215°C (419°F), the FCV starts to reduce the flow.

question: Under what condition will the pack Flow Control Valve (FCV) automatically close?

options.a: During an engine start sequence on either the same or opposite side (if X-bleed is open)
options.b: When cabin altitude reaches 10,000 ft
options.c: Whenever the ram air inlet flap is fully closed

justification: Each pack FCV is automatically closed during either a same side engine start sequence or an opposite side engine start sequence, if the crossbleed valve is detected open.

question: What happens to the pack FCV when the compressor outlet temperature reaches 260°C while the aircraft is on the ground?

options.a: The FCV remains open but triggers an ECAM warning
options.b: The ACSC closes the FCV and the FAULT light on the pack PB illuminates
options.c: The pack continues to operate in a low-flow backup mode

justification: At a temperature of 260°C and with the aircraft on ground, the ACSC will close the FCV and send a signal to illuminate the FAULT light in the related pack pushbutton switch.

question: What is the purpose of the water injector in the pack cooling cycle?

options.a: To provide moisture to the cabin during high altitude flight
options.b: To inject extracted water into the ram air duct to increase cooling efficiency of the heat exchangers
options.c: To prevent ice formation on the compressor blades

justification: Water extracted from the air flow is injected into the ram air duct through the water injector to increase the cooling efficiency of the primary and main heat exchangers.

question: For dispatch per the MEL with a failed pack Flow Control Valve (FCV), in what position must the valve be secured?

options.b: CLOSED
options.c: MID-TRANSIT

justification: Per the MEL/Deactivation procedure, if a pack FCV fails, it must be secured in the CLOSED position for dispatch.

question: What type of outflow valve is used in the A320 family pressurization system?

options.b: Dual gate type valve
options.c: Single butterfly flap valve

justification: Pressurization is done by a dual gate type outflow valve.

question: Where are the safety valves located on the aircraft?

options.b: On the rear pressure bulkhead
options.c: Next to the outflow valve in the belly fairing

justification: To protect the fuselage against excessive pressure, safety valves are installed on the rear pressure bulkhead.

question: How do the two Cabin Pressure Controllers (CPCs) operate during flight?

options.b: Only one operates at a time, and they alternate each flight
options.c: CPC 1 handles the cockpit while CPC 2 handles the cabin

justification: Only one system operates at a time with the other acting as backup. The system in command will alternate each flight.

question: What is the function of the Residual Pressure Control Unit (RPCU)?

options.a: It regulates the cabin pressure during emergency electrical configuration
options.b: It prevents residual pressure in the cabin on the ground by automatically controlling the outflow valve
options.c: It monitors the safety valves and reports their position to the ECAM

justification: The RPCU prevents residual pressure in the cabin and takes over control of the outflow valve automatically on the ground to prevent any door violent opening.

question: How many electrical motors operate the outflow valve assembly?

options.b: Two motors: one for AUTO and one for MANUAL
options.c: Three motors: two for automatic mode and one for manual mode

justification: The outflow valve is operated by three electrical motors: two for the automatic mode and one for the manual mode.

question: At what cabin altitude does the MASTER WARN trigger if the cabin altitude increases excessively?
justification: The manual states if cabin altitude increases, at 9,550 ft, the MASTER WARN comes on.

question: What action occurs automatically when the cabin altitude reaches 11,300 ft?

options.a: The outflow valve is driven fully closed
options.b: Passenger signs are activated
options.c: The oxygen masks are dropped

justification: If cabin altitude increases, at 11,300 ft, passenger signs are activated.

question: What is the purpose of the pressure switch installed in each electronic actuator of the outflow valve?

options.a: To close the outflow valve if cabin altitude exceeds 15,000 ft in automatic mode
options.b: To override the RPCU during takeoff power application
options.c: To signal the EIU to increase engine idle speed

justification: A pressure switch is installed in each electronic actuator; it closes the applicable outflow valve in case of cabin altitude above 15,000 ft (only in automatic mode).

question: Which aircraft computer provides cruise flight level and landing field elevation data to the CPCs?

options.b: Flight Management and Guidance Computer (FMGC)
options.c: Engine Interface Unit (EIU)

justification: Each Flight Management and Guidance Computer (FMGC) sends cruise flight level and landing field elevation data to both controllers.

question: In what specific condition will the RPCU drive the outflow valve fully open using Motor 3?

options.a: Whenever the DITCHING pushbutton is released
options.b: On ground, if both landing gears are compressed, both Master Switches are OFF or speed < 100kt, and CPCs are inoperative
options.c: In flight if the cabin altitude exceeds 15,000 ft

justification: The RPCU drives the OFV to the fully open position via Motor 3 when ground conditions are met (gears compressed, master switches OFF or speed < 100kts) and the cabin pressurization system is in manual mode or both CPCs are inoperative.

question: Which computer controls the configuration of the skin valves and fans in the avionics ventilation system?

options.b: Avionics Equipment Ventilation Computer (AEVC)
options.c: Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC)

justification: The AEVC controls the fans and the configuration of the skin valves in the avionics ventilation system.

question: How many primary skin air valves are there in the avionics ventilation system?

options.b: Two valves: an inlet valve on the LH side and an outlet valve on the RH side
options.c: Three valves: Inlet, Outlet, and Bypass

justification: The skin air inlet valve is on the LH side of the fuselage, and the skin air outlet valve is on the RH side.

question: What is the configuration of the avionics ventilation system in 'Open Circuit' mode?

options.a: Air is recirculated through a skin heat exchanger
options.b: Ambient air is drawn in through the inlet valve and extracted air is blown overboard through the outlet valve
options.c: Air is cooled by the AC packs and then dumped overboard

justification: In open circuit configuration, ambient air is drawn through the skin air inlet valve by the blower fan and extracted directly overboard by the extraction fan.

question: When does the avionics ventilation system typically operate in the 'Closed Circuit' configuration?

options.a: Always when the aircraft is on the ground regardless of temperature
options.b: In flight or on ground when the external air temperature is low
options.c: Only during smoke removal procedures

justification: The closed circuit is used in flight or if there is low external air temperature on the ground.

question: What happens to the blower and extraction fans when the aircraft electrical system is supplied?

options.a: They operate only when the engines are running
options.b: They operate continuously
options.c: They are controlled manually by the pilots via the overhead panel

justification: These fans operate continuously while the aircraft electrical system is supplied.

question: What is the purpose of the 'Intermediate' circuit configuration in the avionics ventilation system?

options.a: To provide maximum cooling during takeoff
options.b: It is a partially open configuration used when skin temperature is high to expel some air overboard
options.c: To bypass the skin heat exchanger if it becomes clogged

justification: In partially open (intermediate) circuit configuration, the inlet is closed and the outlet is open (small flap only) to expel some extracted air overboard when temperature thresholds are met.

question: What ground warning is triggered if a low flow or high duct temperature (62°C) is detected in the avionics ventilation system?

options.a: A MASTER WARN on the glareshield
options.b: An external horn activation and amber ADIRU & AVNCS VENT lights on the external power receptacle
options.c: Automatic shutdown of all non-essential avionics

justification: On the ground, low flow or high duct temperature (62°C) causes the ADIRU and AVNCS VENT lights to come on amber on the external power receptacle accompanied by horn activation.

question: To prevent water ingestion into the avionics ventilation system during heavy rain on the ground, what action should be taken?

options.a: Select the BLOWER PB to OFF
options.b: Select the EXTRACT PB to OVRD to put the system in CLOSED configuration
options.c: Open the avionics bay doors to allow natural drainage

justification: To prevent water ingestion, the ventilation system should be put in the CLOSED configuration by selecting the EXTRACT pushbutton to OverRriDe (OVRD).

question: In the event of a skin air inlet valve failure, what is the mandatory deactivation procedure for flight?

options.a: Deactivate it CLOSED and deactivate the Conditioned Air Inlet Valve to OPEN
options.b: Deactivate it OPEN and disable the blower fan
options.c: Deactivate it in the PARTIAL-OPEN position

justification: If the Skin Air Inlet Valve fails, it may be deactivated CLOSED. In this case, the Conditioned Air Inlet Valve must be deactivated OPEN to allow supplemental cooling from the cockpit AC supply.

question: If the skin air outlet valve is deactivated in the PARTIAL-OPEN position, which other valve must be deactivated into the OPEN position?

options.a: The air conditioning inlet bypass valve
options.b: The skin exchanger isolation valve
options.c: The pack flow control valve

justification: When the Skin Air Outlet Valve is deactivated PARTIALLY OPEN, the Skin exchanger Isolation Valve must be deactivated into the OPEN position.

question: How many fire extinguisher bottles are installed for each engine in the pylon?

options.b: Two bottles
options.c: Three bottles

justification: Each engine has 2 fire bottles installed in the pylon.

question: Which unit is responsible for monitoring the fire detection loops and sending FIRE signals to the FWC?

options.b: The Fire Detection Unit (FDU)
options.c: The Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC)

justification: The two loops are monitored by each Fire Detection Unit (FDU), which sends FIRE and FAULT signals to the FWC.

question: What characterizes the 'ALARM' state in a gas-type fire detector?

options.a: A loss of gas pressure due to a pipe fracture
options.b: The expansion of helium gas by average temperature or release of hydrogen from the hybrid core by local flame
options.c: A short circuit in the electrical sensing element

justification: In ALARM state, average temperature expands helium which closes the ALARM switch, or local flame releases active gas (hydrogen) from the core which closes the switch.

question: Under what condition will the FDU generate a fire warning signal in a dual-loop configuration?

options.a: Only when both Loop A and Loop B detect fire simultaneously
options.b: When fire is detected on both loops, or one loop detects fire and the other is faulty
options.c: When fire is detected on either loop regardless of the status of the other

justification: A fire warning is generated if: fire on A AND fire on B; fire on A AND fault on B; fault on A AND fire on B; or both loops fault within 5 seconds.

question: What triggers a 'LOOP FAULT' warning in the cockpit?

options.a: Detection of a single loop fire for more than 16 seconds while the other is normal
options.b: Immediate detection of any single loop failure
options.c: Activation of the TEST pushbutton while in flight

justification: A loop fault is generated for electrical failure, integrity failure, or if a single loop detects fire for more than 16 seconds while the other is normal.

question: Releasing the ENGINE FIRE pushbutton out triggers several isolation actions. Which pneumatic system valves are closed as a result?

options.b: The engine bleed valve and the pack flow control valve
options.c: The crossbleed valve and all trim air valves

justification: Pneumatically, releasing the fire PB out closes the engine bleed valve and the pack flow control valve.

question: During the fire extinguishing procedure in flight, why is a 10-second delay recommended before pressing AGENT 1?

options.a: To allow the fire detection system to re-verify the fire
options.b: To reduce engine windmilling and nacelle ventilation, increasing agent effect
options.c: To allow the EIU to complete the engine shutdown cycle

justification: A 10-second wait is required to reduce engine windmilling and nacelle ventilation, which increases the agent effect.

question: When performing maintenance with the FIRE pushbutton released out, what must be done to prevent accidental bottle discharge?

options.b: Pull both squib circuit breakers (C/Bs)
options.c: Depressurize the pneumatic system

justification: Maintenance tips state that squibs are supplied by the HOT bus; to protect against discharge when the fire PB is out, you must pull both squib C/Bs.

question: What must be done before working on a fire extinguishing bottle during removal?

options.a: Discharge the remaining agent into a recovery tank
options.b: Remove the explosive cartridges (squibs)
options.c: Apply standard oil to the threads for easier removal

justification: Fire bottle cartridges are explosive and must be removed before working on the bottle.

question: In the event of an APU fire on the ground, what automatic action occurs?

options.a: The APU shuts down and the fire extinguisher bottle discharges after a 3-second delay
options.b: The APU shuts down immediately but the crew must discharge the agent manually
options.c: The fire detection system triggers the external horn only

justification: When an APU fire is detected on ground, the APU shuts down automatically and the fire extinguishing system is automatically triggered (3 seconds after shutdown initiated by ECB).

question: Which wing slats are protected by the hot anti-icing air system?

options.b: The three outboard slats (3, 4, and 5)
options.c: Slats 1 and 2 only

justification: Hot air from the pneumatic system is provided for the anti-icing of the three outboard leading edge slats (3, 4 and 5) of each wing.

question: Where are the wing anti-ice control valves located?

options.b: In each wing leading-edge outboard of the engine pylons
options.c: In the engine pylon downstream of the precooler

justification: Two wing anti-ice control-valves are installed, one in each wing leading-edge outboard of the engine pylons.

question: What happens when the WING Anti-Ice PB is selected ON while the aircraft is on the ground?

options.a: The valves open indefinitely to allow for full system testing
options.b: A time-delay relay limits the opening of the valves to 30 seconds
options.c: The system is inhibited until takeoff power is applied

justification: On the ground for test functions, a time-delay relay limits the opening of the valve to 30 seconds when the pushbutton switch is selected ON.

question: What is the approximate regulated pressure provided by the anti-ice control valves to the wing slats?

options.b: 44 psi
options.c: 75 psi

justification: The anti-ice control valves regulate the anti-icing pressure to approximately 23 psi.

question: Which component manages the bleed air and stores failure data for the Wing Anti-Ice (WAI) system?

options.b: The Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC)
options.c: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU)

justification: The Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC) 1 and 2 are interfacing with signals from the wing ice protection system to monitor the system, manage bleed air, and store failure data.

question: If the wing anti-ice valve is deactivated OPEN per the MEL, what is the required operational restriction?

options.a: The aircraft is limited to 20,000 ft altitude
options.b: The associated engine bleed switch must be selected OFF until after takeoff
options.c: Wing anti-ice must be used continuously throughout the flight

justification: If the valve is deactivated OPEN, the associated engine bleed switch must be selected OFF until after takeoff. A flight manual performance penalty is applied.

question: What is the penalty for fuel consumption when an aircraft is dispatched with a wing anti-ice valve deactivated in the OPEN position?

options.b: 3% increase
options.c: 5% increase

justification: If the valve is deactivated OPEN... a flight manual performance penalty is applied (fuel consumption is increased by 1%).

question: Can the aircraft be flown into icing conditions if a wing anti-ice valve is deactivated CLOSED?

options.a: Yes, provided the other wing's anti-ice is operational
options.b: No, the aircraft may not be flown into icing conditions
options.c: Only if the flight is below 10,000 ft

justification: If the valve is deactivated CLOSED, the aircraft may not be flown into icing conditions.

question: What is the function of the restrictor located downstream from the wing anti-ice control valve?

options.a: To decrease pressure from 44 psi to 23 psi
options.b: To adjust airflow and limit flow in case of a distribution duct rupture
options.c: To prevent backflow from the APU bleed system

justification: A restrictor located downstream from the control valve adjusts the airflow. It also limits the flow in case of rupture of a distribution duct.

question: What triggers the illumination of the FAULT light on the WING Anti-Ice PB?

options.a: Whenever the system is operating on the ground
options.b: During valve transit or in case of disagreement between valve position and system selection
options.c: Only when the BMC 1 has failed

justification: The WAI P/BSW acquires a discrete signal... for the illumination of the FAULT light, during either valves transit or in case of disagreement between valves position and system selection.

question: Which sensors are included in the probe ice protection system?

options.a: Pitot probes and static ports only
options.b: AOA sensors, pitot probes, static ports, and TAT probes
options.c: Wing slat sensors and engine intake sensors

justification: Ice protection of the Angle Of Attack (AOA) sensors, pitot probes, static ports, and Total Air Temperature (TAT) probes is achieved by electrical heating.

question: How many Probe Heat Computers (PHCs) are installed on the aircraft?

options.b: Two computers (Left and Right)
options.c: Three computers (CAPT, F/O, and STBY)

justification: The CAPT, F/O and STBY systems are independent. Each one includes a Probe Heat Computer (PHC).

question: When does probe and static port heating come on automatically?

options.a: Immediately upon battery power being switched ON
options.b: When at least one engine is running
options.c: Only when the aircraft is in flight

justification: The probes and static ports heating come on automatically when at least one engine is running.

question: What is the status of TAT heating when the aircraft is on the ground?

options.b: Cut off automatically
options.c: Always operating at full power

justification: On ground, pitot heating is reduced and TAT heating is cut off.

question: What power source supplies the windshield heating elements?

options.b: 115 VAC single phase
options.c: 200 VAC (dual phase 115 VAC)

justification: The windshield is supplied with 200 VAC (dual phase 115 V AC).

question: What is the consequence of pulling a Probe Heat Computer (PHC) power supply circuit breaker?

options.a: The heating for that system is completely lost
options.b: The related probes and static ports will be fully heated
options.c: The ADIRU associated with that PHC will fail

justification: If you pull the PHC power supplied C/B, the related probes and static ports will be fully heated.

question: What temperature regulation range does the Window Heat Computer (WHC) maintain for the cockpit windows?
justification: The WHC supplies independent temperature regulation between 35 and 42°C (95 and 107.6°F).

question: For safety, at what temperature threshold will the WHC cut off window heating?
justification: For safety: heating is cut off if temperature reaches +/-60°C (140 or -76°F).

question: What maintenance action is required if a primary windshield temperature sensor fails?

options.a: The entire windshield must be replaced
options.b: The connectors must be swapped to the spare sensor
options.c: The WHC must be reprogrammed to ignore the failed sensor

justification: Each windshield has three loop sensors; only one can be connected at a time. If that sensor fails, maintenance has to swap the connectors to the spare sensor.

question: What is the effect on the windshield heating level when the aircraft moves from ground to flight configuration?

options.a: It switches from AC to DC heating
options.b: It switches from low power to high power heating
options.c: Heating is automatically cut off to prevent over-temperature

justification: The windshield heating operates at low power on the ground and high power in flight.

question: Where is the high-pressure oxygen cylinder for the flight crew located?

options.b: In the L/H avionics compartment
options.c: In the cockpit behind the captain's seat

justification: The cylinder is installed in a cradle with two quick-release clamps in the L/H avionics compartment.

question: What is the function of the overboard discharge indicator on the aircraft skin?

options.a: To indicate that the oxygen cylinder is being filled
options.b: To show that the cylinder has discharged due to overpressure if the green disk is missing
options.c: To vent excess cabin air during depressurization

justification: An overboard green discharge indicator is connected to the safety outlets. If there is overpressure, the green disk blows out.

question: What are the two pressure stages provided by the pressure regulator transmitter assembly?

options.a: A high-pressure stage for filling and a low-pressure stage for breathing
options.b: A high-pressure stage for ECAM indication and a low-pressure stage for distribution
options.c: A mechanical stage for the gauge and an electrical stage for the computer

justification: It includes a high-pressure stage with an integrated pressure transducer for ECAM indication and a low-pressure stage (regulating at 65 to 94 psig).

question: What is the difference between the 'Normal' and '100%' positions on the crew oxygen mask regulator?

options.a: Normal provides 100% oxygen while 100% provides a mixture
options.b: Normal provides a mixture of cabin air and oxygen, while 100% provides pure oxygen
options.c: Normal is for low altitude and 100% is for high altitude

justification: In the Normal position, the user breathes a mixture of cabin air and oxygen. When the selector is in the 100% position, the user will breathe pure oxygen.

question: How is oxygen flow indicated to the crew member during mask use?

options.b: By a yellow blinker showing and an OXY ON flag on the stowage box door
options.c: By a pressure drop on the cockpit indicator

justification: Oxygen flow is indicated by the blinker showing yellow and an OXY ON flag, which appears on the left door when closed.

question: What happens if the crew oxygen supply pressure decreases below 50 psi?

options.b: A REGUL LO PR warning is transmitted to the ECAM DOOR/OXY page
options.c: The passenger oxygen masks are dropped automatically

justification: The pressure switch operates when the oxygen supply pressure decreases to 50 psi and transmits a warning signal REGUL LO PR to the ECAM.

question: What is the threshold for an amber half-frame (advisory) for oxygen pressure on the ECAM for a 77 cuft bottle?

options.b: 800 psi
options.c: 1500 psi

justification: If the pressure is less than 1500 PSI for a 77 cuft bottle, an amber half frame (advisory) is shown for information.

question: What safety precaution must be strictly observed regarding hydrocarbons near oxygen components?

options.a: Hydrocarbons can be used as thread lubricants if applied sparingly
options.b: Keep all hydrocarbons away as oxygen becomes explosive when it touches them
options.c: Hydrocarbons only react with oxygen at temperatures above 120°C

justification: The manual explicitly warns to keep all hydrocarbons away from all sources of oxygen as it becomes explosive upon contact.

question: What is the purpose of the 'emergency rotation knob' on the oxygen mask regulator?

options.a: To vent the mask if smoke enters the hood
options.b: To supply 100% oxygen at a permanent positive pressure
options.c: To manually release the mask from the stowage box

justification: When the emergency rotation knob is rotated, the mask regulator supplies 100% of oxygen at a permanent positive pressure.

question: During the Daily Check, what must be verified on the cockpit oxygen mask stowage box after testing?

options.a: The OXY ON flag must be visible
options.b: The NORMAL/100% selector must be locked in the 100% position
options.c: The oxygen supply valve must be manually closed

justification: When the tests are completed, make sure that the NORMAL / 100% selector is locked in the 100% position.

question: What are the two common supply durations for chemical oxygen generators used in the passenger system?

options.b: 15 minutes or 22 minutes
options.c: 22 minutes or 30 minutes

justification: There are two types of chemical generators that supply oxygen for 15 minutes or 22 minutes.

question: What type of oxygen system is commonly used in the A319CJ or as an option for longer range operations?

options.b: Gaseous oxygen cylinder assemblies
options.c: Bleed-air based molecular sieve oxygen generators

justification: The manual describes a 'Passenger Gaseous Oxygen SYS' (option) using oxygen cylinder assemblies, often used for large range/ETOPS operations.

question: Which signal automatically triggers the release of the passenger oxygen masks?

options.a: When the cabin altitude reaches 10,000 ft
options.b: When the altitude pressure switch closes at approximately 14,000 ft
options.c: Whenever the ACSC detects a loss of pack flow

justification: The masks fall automatically when the cabin altitude is higher than 14,000 feet, which is triggered when the altitude pressure switch closes.

question: How is the chemical reaction initiated in a passenger oxygen generator?

options.a: By an electrical signal from the CIDS
options.b: By pulling the mask towards the face, which pulls a release pin and activates a firing pin
options.c: By increasing the pressure in the distribution manifold

justification: When the first user pulls the mask towards his face, the release pin starts the chemical generation by hitting a percussion cap.

question: What is the function of the Quantity Calculation and Control Unit (QCCU) in the gaseous oxygen system?

options.a: It controls the rate of flow to the passenger masks based on the number of occupants
options.b: It monitors oxygen pressure and sends non-compensated pressure to the fill panel and adjusted pressure to the POXIP
options.c: It automatically refills the cylinders during flight from an onboard compressor

justification: The QCCU monitors pressure from transmitters and the temperature transducer, sending arithmetic average pressure to the fill panel and temperature adjusted pressure to the POXIP.

question: If both detectors in one cargo cavity are faulty, what is the MEL requirement for dispatch?

options.a: The aircraft may be dispatched only if the other cargo compartment is operational
options.b: The aircraft may be dispatched with the compartment empty or containing no inflammable materials
options.c: Dispatch is not permitted with two failed detectors in the same cavity

justification: If both detectors in one cavity are faulty... the aircraft may be dispatched with the compartment empty... or as long as the compartment does not contain inflammable or combustible materials.

question: What occurs when the oxygen system 'TMR RESET' pushbutton is pressed on the maintenance panel?

options.a: The oxygen chemical generators are reset for another cycle
options.b: The electrical circuit is reset, the SYS ON indicator goes off and the PA announcement stops
options.c: The oxygen masks are retracted into their containers

justification: When the TMR RESET pushbutton is pushed, the ON light comes on, the indicator light SYS ON goes off and the taped announcement stops.

question: How are the passenger oxygen container doors opened manually if the electrical system fails?

options.a: By pulling the passenger address handset
options.b: Using a manual release tool
options.c: By increasing cabin pressure beyond the differential limit

justification: The door can be opened manually with a release tool if there is a failure of the container door opening system.

question: Which color indication on a chemical oxygen generator's thermal indicator shows that it has been used (burned out)?

options.b: Black or Blue
options.c: Green or White

justification: According to the manual, Black or Blue indicates the oxygen generator has been burned out, while Yellow or Pink indicates it is new.

question: What is the purpose of the 'door stops' installed on passenger oxygen container doors?

options.a: To hold the door open for extra ventilation on the ground
options.b: To allow for an operational test of the mask release system without the masks falling out
options.c: To prevent the doors from hitting passengers in the event of an automatic deployment

justification: Manually operated door stops are used to do an operational test of the mask release system. In the test position, the doors will not open fully and the masks will not fall out.

question: What are the two primary sub-systems of the Fuel Tank Inerting System (FTIS)?

options.a: The Nitrogen Supply System and the Oxygen Extraction System
options.b: The Conditioned Service Air System (CSAS) and the Inert Gas Generation System (IGGS)
options.c: The Bleed Air Management System and the Fuel Cooling System

justification: The FTIS includes two sub-systems: The Conditioned Service Air System (CSAS) and the Inert Gas Generation System (IGGS).

question: Which component is considered the core of the IGGS and is responsible for removing oxygen from the compressed air stream?

options.b: The Air Separation Module (ASM)
options.c: The Dual Flow Shut Off Valve (DFSOV)

justification: The ASM is the core of the Inert Gas Generation System. It removes oxygen from the compressed air stream.

question: What products are generated by the Air Separation Module (ASM) from the input conditioned air?

options.b: Nitrogen Enriched Air (NEA) and Oxygen Enriched Air (OEA)
options.c: Cooling air and HP turbine air

justification: The IGGS uses an Air Separation Module (ASM) to divide the conditioned air stream into Nitrogen Enriched Air (NEA) and Oxygen Enriched Air (OEA).

question: Where is the Oxygen Enriched Air (OEA) produced by the ASM sent?

options.a: To the cabin for supplemental oxygen
options.b: Overboard through an outlet on the HPGC door
options.c: Into the engine intake for combustion augmentation

justification: The OEA is sent overboard through an outlet on the HPGC door.

question: What is the function of the Dual Flow Shut Off Valve (DFSOV)?

options.a: It regulates the temperature of the CSAS heat exchanger
options.b: It controls the NEA flow to the center tank and isolates the IGGS from the fuel tank in abnormal operation
options.c: It divides the bleed air flow between the two engines

justification: The DFSOV controls the NEA flow to the center tank, lets the system change between flow rates, and isolates the IGGS from the fuel tank if an abnormal operation occurs.

question: At what oxygen rate detected by the oxygen sensor will the ICU close the IGGS Isolation Gate Valve and the DFSOV?

options.b: Higher than 12%
options.c: Higher than 21%

justification: If the oxygen sensor senses an oxygen rate higher than 12%, the ICU de-energizes the solenoids to close the IGGS Isolation Gate Valve and the DFSOV.

question: Which component prevents fuel ingress from the fuel tank back into the IGGS?

options.b: The Dual Flapper Check Valve
options.c: The DFSOV

justification: A Dual Flapper Check Valve makes a double barrier to the possible back-flow of fuel from the fuel tank back to the IGGS.

question: What temperature is the CSAS heat exchanger designed to produce for the IGGS input?
justification: The air temperature is decreased by the CSAS heat exchanger to get a temperature of 60°C +/- 6°C.

question: According to the MEL, how long can the aircraft be dispatched with the CSAS system unserviceable?

options.b: 10 days
options.c: 30 days

justification: The MEL tells that the A/C can be dispatched with the system unserviceable for 10 days with no maintenance procedure.

question: What data does the ADIRU 1 provide to the Inerting Gas Generation System Controller Unit (ICU)?

options.b: Standard Altitude, True Airspeed, Total Air Temperature and Altitude Rate
options.c: Barometric correction and static pressure only

justification: The ADIRU 1 supplies Standard Altitude, True Airspeed, Total Air Temperature and Altitude Rate signals to the ICU.

question: Which engine is the primary bleed source for the Conditioned Service Air System (CSAS)?

options.b: Engine 2
options.c: The APU

justification: The manual states Engine 1 is the primary bleed source and Eng 2... is the secondary bleed source.

question: Where is the Conditioned Service Air System Controller Unit (CCU) located?

options.b: In the forward electronics rack (90VU) in the avionics compartment
options.c: Near the center fuel tank

justification: The CSAS controller is installed in the FWD electronics rack (90VU) in the avionics compartment.

question: What is the purpose of the Ozone Converter in the CSAS?

options.a: To increase the oxygen content of the bleed air
options.b: To decrease the quantity of ozone in the bleed air to protect IGGS components
options.c: To catalyze the creation of nitrogen for inerting

justification: The ozone converter decreases the quantity of ozone in the bleed air to give protection to the IGGS components.

question: Which aircraft system provides the 'INERT FAULT' status message for maintenance when a failure occurs in the CSAS?

options.b: The Flight Warning System (FWS)
options.c: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU)

justification: The CCU has interfaces with the FWS and CFDS. If a failure occurs, the status message 'INERT FAULT' will come into view.

question: What happens if there is over-pressure or over-temperature in the CSAS output duct?

options.a: The ACSC shuts down the associated engine bleed
options.b: The CSAS isolation valve closes to stop the system
options.c: The bypass valve opens fully to vent the air overboard

justification: If there is over-pressure or over-temperature, the CSAS isolation valve closes to stop the system.

question: Where is the avionics smoke detector located?

options.a: In the blower fan intake duct
options.b: In the ventilation extraction duct
options.c: In the cockpit ceiling panel

justification: The avionics smoke detector is installed in the extraction duct downstream of the avionics equipment.

question: How many smoke detectors are installed in each cavity of the cargo compartments?

options.b: Two detectors
options.c: Four detectors

justification: Each cargo compartment has 2 smoke detectors in each cavity.

question: Which function within the Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS) monitors the cargo smoke detectors?

options.b: The Smoke Detection Function (SDF)
options.c: The Avionics Monitoring Function (AMF)

justification: The cargo compartment smoke detection system is monitored by the Smoke Detection Function (SDF) integrated in the CIDS.

question: What is the result when only one cargo smoke detector detects smoke while the second shows normal operation?

options.a: The smoke warning is immediately activated for safety
options.b: The first detector is declared faulty and no smoke warning is triggered in the cockpit
options.c: The system automatically discharges the fire bottle in that compartment

justification: If the test shows a normal operation of the second detector, the first detector is declared faulty. The result is no smoke warning in the cockpit.

question: In the event of a total loss of the CIDS-SDF function (both directors fail), where is the fault indicated?

options.b: On the Engine and Warning Display (EWD) accompanied by a Single Chime and MASTER CAUT light
options.c: On the PFR (Post Flight Report) only

justification: If the SDF cards in CIDS director 1 and 2 fail, an automatic fault indication is shown on the EWD accompanied by the SC and MASTER CAUT light.

question: Which local warnings are triggered on the CARGO SMOKE panel when smoke is detected in the aft compartment?

options.a: The SMOKE light and the DISCH light illuminate
options.b: The SMOKE light illuminates and the FAULT light on the CARGO HEAT panel comes on
options.c: Only the red MASTER WARN light on the glareshield

justification: In case of detection, the respective SMOKE light comes on... and the isolation valves of the affected compartment close, which causes the ISOL VALVE FAULT light on the CARGO HEAT panel to come on.

question: How long should the cockpit crew allow for the AVIONICS SMOKE warning to disappear after the ventilation system is reconfigured to OVRD?

options.b: 3 minutes
options.c: 5 minutes

justification: After reconfiguration... the cockpit crew should allow 5 minutes for the SMOKE warning to disappear.

question: What is the procedure for manually resetting visual and aural smoke indications in the cabin from the FAP?

options.a: Press the Smoke Reset button on the touchscreen or the SMOKE RESET hard key on the subpanel
options.b: Recycle the cabin intercommunication master switch
options.c: The indications cannot be manually reset and must clear automatically

justification: The visual and aural indications in cabin can be manually reset by pushing the Smoke Reset button on the FAP touchscreen or the SMOKE RESET hard key on the FAP subpanel.

question: Why should the on-board cargo fire extinguisher bottle never be discharged for a smoke warning on the ground?

options.a: The agent is toxic to ground personnel
options.b: A visual inspection must be done first; if fire is confirmed, portable extinguishers must be used
options.c: The cargo doors must be closed for the bottle to be effective

justification: In case of cargo smoke warning on ground you should never discharge the on-board extinguishing bottle. A visual inspection... must be done. If fire is confirmed, portable extinguishers must be used.

question: What action occurs when the 'GEN 1 LINE' pushbutton is set to OFF during an avionics smoke procedure?

options.b: It opens the GEN 1 LINE contactor to isolate a potential smoke source while keeping the generator supplying fuel pumps
options.c: It forces the aircraft into emergency electrical configuration

justification: To isolate the smoke source, the GEN 1 LINE P/BSW is set to OFF. This opens the contactor. Generator 1 keeps on supplying one fuel pump on each wing tank.

question: Where is the engine anti-ice valve located on the engine?

options.a: At the 12 o'clock position on the fan case
options.b: On the lower right hand side of the engine
options.c: On the upper left hand side of the engine core

justification: The engine anti-ice valve is installed on the lower right hand side of the engine.

question: Which engine stage provides the bleed air for the engine anti-ice system on the V2500 engine?

options.b: 7th stage
options.c: 9th stage

justification: Hot air for the engine anti-ice system is supplied by a dedicated HP Compressor (HPC) bleed: on the V2500, 7th stage.

question: What is the fail-safe position of the engine anti-ice valve in the event of a loss of electrical power?

options.b: OPEN
options.c: LAST POSITION

justification: The solenoid is energized to CLOSE the valve, so in case of loss of electrical power supply, the valve will go fully open (provided air pressure is available).

question: How does the NAI (Nacelle Anti-Icing) system affect engine performance when selected ON?

options.a: It increases the maximum N1 limit to compensate for drag
options.b: It decreases the maximum N1 or EPR limit via the FADEC to account for bleed demand
options.c: It has no effect on engine power limits

justification: The additional bleed demand decreases the maximum N1 (CFM/PW) and maximum EPR limit (V2500) via the FADEC.

question: Which component is responsible for bleed management when the engine Anti-Ice (A.ICE) system is switched ON?

options.b: Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC) 1
options.c: Full Authority Digital Engine Control (FADEC)

justification: The Air Conditioning System Controller (ACSC) 1 is responsible for the bleed management when the engine Anti Ice (A.ICE) system is switched ON.

question: What is the procedure for manually deactivating an engine anti-ice valve into the OPEN position for the CFM56 engine?

options.a: Set FADEC ground power OFF, open RH fan cowl, move manual override and lock with a pin
options.b: Disconnect the electrical plug and cap the sense line
options.c: Rotate the override lever until the green indicator is visible and safety wire it

justification: The procedure is: FADEC ground power OFF, open RH fan cowl, move the manual override to the required position and lock in place with the locking pin.

question: When an engine anti-ice valve is deactivated in the OPEN position, which of the following is true?

options.a: There are no flight performance penalties
options.b: A Flight Manual performance penalty must be applied (takeoff weight, speeds, fuel consumption)
options.c: The aircraft is limited to a maximum altitude of 10,000 ft

justification: If the valve is deactivated OPEN, a Flight Manual performance penalty must be applied. Based on temperature and altitude, max weight, takeoff speeds and fuel consumption will be adjusted.

question: How is the air intake anti-ice valve locked manually on the PW6000 engine?

options.b: With a dedicated locking lever in the OPEN or CLOSED position
options.c: By tightening a setscrew on the valve body

justification: For PW6000 engines, the air intake anti-ice valve is locked manually with the locking lever in the OPEN position or the CLOSED position.

question: What triggers the 'FAULT' light on the engine anti-ice pushbutton?

options.a: Only when the valve is in the OPEN position on the ground
options.b: During valve transit or in case of disagreement between valve position and system selection
options.c: Whenever engine oil pressure is low

justification: The 'FAULT' light comes on either during valve transit or in case of disagreement between valve position and system selection.

question: What is the function of the restrictor plate in the CFM56 TECH INSERTION engine anti-ice system?

options.a: To limit the maximum temperature to 60°C
options.b: To comply with certification requirements in case of duct rupture or failure
options.c: To increase the air pressure for better ice removal

justification: The modified NAI supply duct with the restrictor plate... complies with the certification requirement in case of duct rupture or failure.

question: How is the rain repellent liquid stored on the aircraft?

options.a: In a gravity-fed reservoir under the cockpit floor
options.b: In a pressurized bottle (can) directly attached to a pressure gage
options.c: It is mixed with the windshield washer fluid in a central tank

justification: The rain repellent fluid used is packaged in a nitrogen-pressurized can. The can is directly attached to the rain repellent fluid gage.

question: What prevents the rain repellent spray nozzles from clogging?

options.b: They are permanently purged by air from the cabin hot air supply
options.c: They are automatically cleaned by the windshield wipers

justification: The spray nozzles are permanently purged by air from cabin hot air supply.

question: What occurs when the RAIN RPLNT pushbutton is pressed?

options.a: The fluid is sprayed continuously until the button is released
options.b: A time-controlled solenoid valve opens to release a measured quantity of fluid
options.c: The windshield wipers automatically move to the FAST position

justification: Upon actuation of the P/B, the time-controlled solenoid valve... releases out fluid to the spray nozzle for a preset period of time.

question: Are the CAPT and F/O rain repellent spray nozzles interchangeable?

options.b: No, they are symmetrical but identified by red (CAPT) and yellow (F/O) paint marks
options.c: Only on the A318 and A319 models

justification: The spray nozzles are symmetrical but not interchangeable: the CAPT spray nozzle is identified with red paint mark, the F/O spray nozzle is identified with yellow paint mark.

question: Under what ground condition is the rain repellent system inhibited?

options.a: When the parking brake is ON
options.b: When both engines are shut down
options.c: Whenever the ambient temperature is below 0°C

justification: On ground, the rain repellent system is inhibited when both engines are shut down.

question: What must be done if rain repellent fluid accidentally gets on the aircraft structure?

options.a: Wait for it to dry as it is non-corrosive
options.b: Wash it off immediately with soap and water
options.c: Apply a neutralizing acid solution

justification: If the fluid gets on the A/C structure, wash it off immediately with soap and water.

question: Is it permissible to apply rain repellent fluid on a dry windshield?

options.a: Yes, to prevent initial rain adhesion
options.b: No, do not apply the rain repellent fluid on a dry surface
options.c: Only during ground test procedures

justification: The manual provides a CAUTION: Do not apply the rain repellent fluid on a dry surface.

question: When should a rain repellent bottle be replaced based on the pressure gage?

options.a: When the needle enters the red range
options.b: When the needle is in the yellow range or the can is completely empty
options.c: Every 3000 flight hours regardless of pressure

justification: When the needle is in the yellow range, or the can is completely empty, the bottle should be replaced.

question: What is the procedure for optional deactivation of the rain repellent system?

options.a: The bottle must be removed and the C/B pulled, safetied, and tagged
options.b: The spray nozzles must be capped and the fluid line drained
options.c: The RAIN RPLNT pushbutton must be safety-wired in the OUT position

justification: For deactivation, the rain repellent bottle has been removed and C/B pulled, safetied and tagged.

question: Which button is used when a new rain repellent can is installed?

options.b: The purge pushbutton
options.c: The TMR RESET pushbutton

justification: A purge P/B is used when the can is replaced.

question: What is the purpose of electrical heating in the drain masts?

options.a: To speed up the dumping of waste water
options.b: To protect drain masts against ice formation
options.c: To provide extra heating for the aft cargo compartment

justification: To protect drain masts against ice formation, electrical heating... is supplied.

question: Where are the two primary drain masts located on the aircraft?

options.b: On the lower fuselage forward and aft sections
options.c: On the vertical stabilizer

justification: There are two Drain Masts located on the lower fuselage forward and aft sections.

question: What components control the heating of the forward and aft drain masts?

options.b: Two Control Units (CUs) located in the cargo compartments
options.c: The AEVC

justification: Two Control Units, located in the cargo compartments, control the Heating of the FWD and AFT Drain Masts.

question: At what temperature range does the Control Unit (CU) regulate the drain mast tube heating?

options.b: Between 6°C (43°F) and 10°C (50°F)
options.c: Between 35°C and 42°C

justification: Each CU regulates the heating temperature of the associated drain mast tube between 6°C (43°F) and 10°C (50°F).

question: Where is the drain mast system status sent for cockpit/cabin indication?

options.a: To the Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS)
options.b: To the Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS) for indication on the FAP
options.c: To the Engine Interface Unit (EIU)

justification: The system status is sent to the Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS) for indication on the Flight Attendant Panel (FAP).

question: What backup regulation exists in the drain mast if the normal temperature control fails?

options.a: A secondary Control Unit (CU) takes over
options.b: A thermal switch opening at 120°C (250°F)
options.c: The system is powered by the DC system instead of AC

justification: The AC power supply line... is installed with a thermal switch opening at 120°C (250°F). It will regulate the temperature in case of normal temperature control failure.

question: During a functional test on the CU front face, how can you tell if the test is satisfactory?

options.b: The Heater (HTR) and CU lights are ON as long as the TEST P/BSW is pressed
options.c: The ECAM triggers a 'DRAIN MAST OK' message

justification: If the test is satisfactory... on the front face of the CU, the HTR and CU lights are ON as long as the associated TEST P/BSW is pressed in.

question: If the drain mast heater fails, can the aircraft be dispatched per the MEL?

options.a: No, it is a 'No-Go' item due to environmental hazard
options.b: Yes, but the water supply to the affected lavatory/galley must be shut off and the lavatory secured
options.c: Yes, provided the flight is under 15,000 ft

justification: The aircraft may be dispatched per Minimum Equipment List with the drain mast heater inoperative. The water supply to the LAV(s) and galley which use the failed drain mast must be shut off.

question: Where is the drain mast failure information indicated to the cabin crew?

options.a: On the CIDS Director status page
options.b: By a CIDS CAUTION light on the FAP and a message in the SYSTEM INFO page
options.c: On the cockpit landing gear control panel

justification: The failure... is indicated on the FAP by a CIDS CAUTION light... and can be seen on the SYSTEM INFO page.

question: What message is displayed on the MCDU during a successful drain mast system test?

options.b: TEST OK
options.c: HEATING VALID

justification: To perform a complete test... one from the MCDU... on the MCDU, the message 'TEST OK' is displayed.

question: Which sections of the aircraft have potable and waste water lines protected by electrical heating?

options.b: Sections 13 and 14
options.c: Sections 19 and 20

justification: The potable and waste water lines in sections 13 and 14 are insulated and electrically heated.

question: Where is the optional air stop drain valve installed?

options.a: On the fuel tank vent line
options.b: On the forward and aft cargo compartment drainage lines
options.c: Inside the potable water storage tank

justification: Two air stop drain valves are installed on the forward and aft cargo compartment drainage lines.

question: When does the water line anti-ice system operate?

options.a: Only when the engines are running
options.b: As soon as the aircraft is electrically supplied
options.c: When selected ON by the flight attendant

justification: Each system operates as soon as the A/C is electrically supplied.

question: How is the heating temperature regulated for each group of heater assemblies?

options.b: By a control unit via their respective sensor
options.c: Manually by adjusting a rheostat on the maintenance panel

justification: Each control unit regulates the temperature range of each group of heater assemblies via their respective sensor.

question: What controls the heating of the air stop drain valves?

options.b: A thermostat and a heater with overheat protection
options.c: The CIDS Director

justification: A thermostat controls the heating and the heater has an overheat protection (approximate operation between 6°C and 13°C).

question: What is the approximate heating operation range for the air stop drain valve?

options.c: 35°C to 42°C

justification: Approximate heating operation is between 6°C (43°F) and 13°C (55°F).

question: At what temperature is overheat protection triggered for the air stop drain valve?
justification: The overheat protection is at 120°C (248°F).

question: What is the indication for a satisfactory manual test of the potable/waste water line heating system?

options.a: A green 'TEST OK' message on the ECAM
options.b: Two green 'OK' LEDs come on the front face of the control unit
options.c: The CIDS CAUTION light on the FAP goes off

justification: On the front face of the control unit, two green 'OK' LEDs come on if the test is satisfactory.

question: Which nipple at the potable water service panel is electrically heated to prevent ice formation?

options.b: The fill/drain nipple (and overflow nipple on A318/319/321)
options.c: The high-pressure vent nipple

justification: The fill/drain nipple... is electrically heated. Note: On the A318/A319/A321 the overflow nipple... is also electrically heated.

question: How is the rinse nipple of the toilet service panel protected against ice?

options.a: By heated air from the avionics ventilation system
options.b: By an electrical heating element controlled by a thermostat
options.c: By using a special non-freezing cleaning solution

justification: The Rinse nipple 21 DV... is electrically heated up and controlled by the thermostat 22 DV.

question: What is the purpose of the dual advisory ice detection system?

options.a: To automatically turn on all anti-ice systems at takeoff
options.b: To provide better detection of icing conditions and allow fuel saving
options.c: To detect ice accumulation on the tail and horizontal stabilizer

justification: The purpose... is to supply: a better detection of icing conditions, and fuel saving by cutting off hot air bleed when no longer necessary.

question: Where are the ice detectors installed on the aircraft?

options.b: On the aircraft skin
options.c: In the cockpit windshield retainer

justification: The dual advisory ice detection system is made of two ice detectors installed on the aircraft skin.

question: What are the two levels of ice detection provided by the system?

options.b: ICE DETECTED and SEVERE ICE DETECTED
options.c: CAUTION and WARNING

justification: Two levels of detection are given: 'ICE DETECTED' and 'SEVERE ICE DETECTED'.

question: How many successive elementary detections are required to trigger a 'SEVERE ICE DETECTED' message?
justification: 'SEVERE ICE DETECTED' corresponds to 7 successive elementary detections.

question: Under what environmental conditions will the ice detection system operate in flight?

options.b: When TAT is below 8°C (46.4°F)
options.c: Only when visibility is less than 1 km

justification: It sends warning messages when the aircraft is in flight... and when Total Air Temperature (TAT) is below 8°C (46.4°F).

question: What triggers the 'ICE DETECT FAULT' signal?

options.a: When only one ice detector fails
options.b: When both ice detectors are faulty
options.c: When the heating element in the detector fails

justification: 'ICE DETECT FAULT' signal occurs when the two ice detectors are faulty.

question: How is the 'SEVERE' ice detection signal and counter reset?

options.b: When the wing anti-ice valves are controlled to open
options.c: By pressing the TMR RESET button on the maintenance panel

justification: When wing anti-ice valves are controlled to open, two ground signals are sent to the ice detectors in order to reset the ice detection counter.

question: Which ECAM message is associated with the 'ICE DETECTED' signal?

options.b: ICE DETECTED
options.c: A.ICE P/BSW FAULT

justification: The ice detectors generate 'ICE DETECTED' signal when engine air intake anti-ice is necessary, which displays the message on the EWD.

question: Where can a class 2 fault message for an ice detector be displayed for maintenance?

options.b: On the MCDU ANTI-ICE ICE DETECTOR 1 or 2 system page
options.c: Only on the Post Flight Report

justification: A class 2 fault message is displayed on the MCDU ANTI-ICE ICE DETECTOR 1 or 2 system page in case of failure.

question: Can the 'ICE DETECTED' warning message be inhibited by crew selection?

options.a: No, it is a priority 1 warning
options.b: Yes, by engine or wing anti-ice selection
options.c: Only when the aircraft is below 1500 ft

justification: These messages can be respectively inhibited by engine or wing anti-ice selection.

question: Where is the visual ice indicator installed on the aircraft?

options.b: In the central retainer of the windshield
options.c: In the engine air intake

justification: A visual ice indicator is installed in the central retainer of the windshield.

question: What material is the visual part of the ice indicator made of?

options.b: Titanium
options.c: Carbon fiber

justification: The ice indicator has a titanium part with openings.

question: Which cockpit switch controls the illumination of the visual ice indicator?

options.b: The ICE IND & STBY COMPASS switch
options.c: The DOME light switch

justification: The indicator light LED... is controlled by the ICE INDicator & STandBY COMPASS switch.

question: What is the power source for the visual ice indicator's LED?

options.b: 28 VDC
options.c: 115 VAC

justification: The indicator light LED is supplied with 28 VDC.

question: What is the purpose of the visual ice indicator?

options.a: To measure the thickness of ice accumulation
options.b: To provide a visual check for icing conditions at night or in dark conditions
options.c: To automatically trigger the wing anti-ice system

justification: It can be illuminated to check for icing conditions at night or in dark conditions.

question: Which ATA chapter covers the Inert Gas Generation System (IGGS)?

options.b: ATA 36
options.c: ATA 47

justification: The Fuel Tank Inerting System (FTIS) includes two sub-systems: The Conditioned Service Air System (CSAS) ATA 21, and the Inert Gas Generation System (IGGS) ATA 47.

question: What is the primary function of the CSAS within the Fuel Tank Inerting System?

options.a: To generate nitrogen from ambient air
options.b: To get hot air from the bleed system and decrease its temperature to a level compatible with the IGGS
options.c: To pump fuel from the center tank to the engines

justification: The CSAS gets hot air from the bleed air system and decreases its temperature to a level compatible with the IGGS sub-system.

question: From where is the bleed air pulled for CSAS operation?

options.a: Directly from the engine pylon HP duct
options.b: From the High Pressure Ground Connector (HPGC) tube
options.c: From the pack discharge outlet

justification: The bleed air is pulled from the High Pressure Ground Connector (HPGC) tube.

question: Which components monitor the temperature and pressure before the air enters the IGGS?

options.a: A single temperature/pressure transducer in the CCU
options.b: A temperature sensor and a pressure sensor on the output duct
options.c: The engine FADEC sensors

justification: On the output duct, a temperature sensor and a pressure sensor monitor the temperature and the pressure before they go into the IGGS.

question: What is the secondary bleed source for the CSAS if Engine 1 is unavailable?

options.b: Engine 2 (through the X-Bleed valve)
options.c: Ram air through the emergency inlet

justification: Engine 1 is the primary bleed source and Eng 2, through the X-Bleed valve, is the secondary bleed source.

question: If a failure of the CSAS system occurs, in which flight phases will the 'INERT FAULT' status message come into view?

options.b: Phases 1 and 10 (Ground phases)
options.c: All phases of flight

justification: If a failure... occurs, the status message 'INERT FAULT' will come into view only in flight phase 1 and 10, for maintenance.

question: Which valve acts as a protection for the system in case of low pressure, over pressure, or over temperature?

options.b: The CSAS isolation valve
options.c: The pack flow control valve

justification: A CSAS isolation valve... is a protection of the system if there is low pressure, over pressure or over temperature.

question: What cooling medium is used in the CSAS heat exchanger to decrease the air temperature?

options.b: Ram air
options.c: Liquid nitrogen

justification: The diagrams for CSAS show that Ram Air is used in the Heat Exchanger to cool the bleed air.

question: How does the CSAS controller perform health monitoring?

options.a: Through manual checks of the ozone converter
options.b: Using its integrated BITE (Built-In Test Equipment) function
options.c: By comparing data with the engine FADEC

justification: The CSAS controller... does the system control and health monitoring BITE.

question: Where is the CSAS system installed in the aircraft?

options.b: On the left hand side of the aircraft belly fairing next to pack no. 1
options.c: In the aft cargo compartment

justification: The Conditioned Service Air System is installed on the left hand side of the aircraft belly fairing next to pack no.1.

question: Which valve is the primary shut-off valve for the air conditioning pack?

options.b: Flow Control Valve (FCV)
options.c: Anti-ice Valve

justification: The Flow Control Valve (FCV) adjusts the flow rate through the pack and is the pack shut-off valve.

question: What is the function of the Air Cycle Machine (ACM) turbine?

options.a: To compress the incoming bleed air
options.b: To convert high pressurized air into rotation and decrease air pressure and temperature
options.c: To separate moisture from the air stream

justification: The ACM turbine converts high pressurized air into rotation... The result is a fast decrease of the air pressure and air temperature.

question: What is the purpose of the reheater in the air conditioning pack cycle?

options.a: To increase the temperature of the air before it enters the cabin
options.b: To vaporize the last remaining water droplets before the air is sent to the ACM turbine
options.c: To prevent the primary heat exchanger from freezing

justification: The REHEATER... is necessary to vaporize the last remaining water droplets before the air is sent to the ACM turbine and to prevent damage to the turbine.

question: How does the air conditioning system determine the airflow going through the pack?

options.a: Using a signal from the compressor speed sensor
options.b: Using the signal from the DIFFERENTIAL PRESS SENSOR at the FCV inlet
options.c: Based on the position of the bypass valve

justification: The ACSC uses the signal from the DIFFERENTIAL PRESS SENSOR to determine the air flow that goes through the pack.

question: What component prevents leakage of air from the distribution system back into the pack when the FCV is closed?

options.b: The Bypass Valve
options.c: The Trim Air Pressure Regulating Valve

justification: The PACK CHECK VALVE, which is downstream of the condenser, stops leakage of air from the distribution system when the FCV is closed.

question: What is the 'Back-up' operating mode for the Pack Flow Control Unit (FCU)?

options.a: The pack is supplied by the opposite engine
options.b: A downstream pressure regulator controls the FCV flow if an FCU component fails
options.c: The pack operates without ram air cooling

justification: If there is a malfunction of an FCU component... the pack operates in back-up mode. In back-up mode, a downstream pressure regulator controls the FCV flow.

question: Under what condition will the air conditioning system default to 'HIGH FLOW'?

options.b: During single pack operation or pack operation with APU bleed air supply
options.c: Whenever the outside air temperature is above 30°C

justification: HIGH FLOW default settings are: during pack operation with the APU bleed air supply, or during single pack operation.

question: What action does the ACSC take if it detects icing at the pack condenser via the Pack Discharge Pressure Sensor?

options.a: It closes the Flow Control Valve (FCV)
options.b: It commands the bypass valve (BYP VLV) to a more open position to let hot air melt the ice
options.c: It switches the pack to backup mode

justification: If the difference... is more than a specified limit... there can be icing at the condenser. This causes the ACSC to command the bypass valve to a more open position.
