question: Which ACSC is responsible for performing the air flow calculation for both packs?

options.b: ACSC 2
options.c: Both ACSCs perform independent calculations

justification: ACSC 1 only does the air flow calculation. The signal is then sent to ACSC 2 for the flow control of pack 2.

question: Where is all BITE data from ACSC 1 transmitted before it reaches the Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU)?

options.a: Directly to the CFDIU via ARINC 429
options.b: Through ACSC 2
options.c: Through the System Data Acquisition Concentrator (SDAC)

justification: The CFDIU is only connected to the ACSC 2. All BITE data of ACSC 1 will be transmitted to ACSC 2 first before it goes to the CFDIU.

question: What is the function of the Trim Air Valves?

options.a: To regulate the total airflow into the cabin
options.b: To optimize zone temperature by adding hot air to the air from the mixer unit
options.c: To bypass the heat exchangers during cold weather

justification: A trim air valve associated with each zone optimizes the temperature by adding hot air... to the air from the mixer unit.

question: Which valve regulates the pressure of the hot air supplied to the trim air valves?

options.b: The trim air Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV)
options.c: The pack flow control valve

justification: Hot air tapped upstream of the packs supplies the trim air valves through a trim air Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV).

question: To what pressure does the trim air PRV regulate the downstream air?

options.b: 4 psi above the cabin pressure
options.c: 6.5 psi above the pack discharge pressure

justification: The trim air PRV regulates the pressure of the air supplied to the trim air valves, 4 psi above the cabin pressure.

question: How are the butterflies of the trim air valves controlled?

options.b: By a stepper motor using the step-counting principle
options.c: Directly by the pilot via mechanical cables

justification: The butterfly of the trim air valves is controlled by a stepper motor. The trim air valve position is determined using the step-counting principle.

question: What is the function of the hot air pressure switch?

options.a: To trigger the passenger oxygen masks
options.b: To signal overpressure to the ACSCs for ECAM display and monitoring
options.c: To automatically switch the ACSC to backup mode

justification: The hot air pressure switch signals overpressure to ACSCs 1 and 2 for ECAM display and the Centralized Fault Display System (CFDS) and monitoring.

question: Under what duct temperature condition will the trim air PRV and all trim air valves close automatically?

options.b: Above 88°C (190°F)
options.c: Above 200°C

justification: The trim air PRV closes... when the temperature of any duct is above 88°C (190°F).

question: What pressure threshold causes ACSC 1 to send a fault signal to the ECAM regarding the hot air system?

options.b: 6.5 psi greater than the cabin pressure
options.c: 57 psi absolute pressure

justification: If pressure in the system is 6.5 psi greater than the cabin pressure, ACSC 1 sends a fault signal to ECAM.

question: What is the consequence when the 'HOT AIR' PB on the air conditioning panel is set to OFF?

options.a: The trim air PRV closes but the trim air valves remain operational
options.b: The trim air PRV solenoid de-energizes and the valve closes
options.c: The pack flow control valves increase flow to compensate

justification: The trim air PRV ON/OFF function solenoid de-energizes when the HOT AIR P/B is set to OFF. This closes the valve.

question: Where are the duct temperature sensors used for zone control located?

options.b: In each of the three supply ducts (Cockpit, FWD, and AFT cabin)
options.c: Directly inside the mixer unit

justification: The diagram show duct temperature sensors (Item 6) are located in the three supply ducts downstream of the trim air valves.

question: How many thermistors does each duct temperature sensor have, and what is their purpose?

options.b: Two thermistors: one for control and one for overheat detection
options.c: Two thermistors: one connected to Lane 1 and the other to Lane 2 of the related ACSC

justification: Each duct temperature sensor has two thermistors, one connected to lane 1 and the other to the second lane of the ACSC.

subtopic: Emergency Ram Air and LP Ground
question: Where is the emergency ram air inlet flap located?

options.b: At the lower LH side of the fuselage
options.c: On the nose section

justification: The A/C has one emergency ram air inlet flap located at the lower LH side of the fuselage.

subtopic: Emergency Ram Air and LP Ground
question: With which other connection does the emergency ram air inlet share a common duct?

options.b: The LP ground connection
options.c: The APU bleed supply

justification: The emergency ram air inlet flap... shares the same duct with the LP ground connection.

subtopic: Emergency Ram Air and LP Ground
question: Under what condition will the emergency ram air inlet flap open in flight?

options.a: Whenever the landing gear is extended
options.b: When the RAM AIR P/B is set to ON and DITCHING is not selected
options.c: Automatically if both packs fail above 20,000 ft

justification: In case of smoke removal or loss of both packs, the RAM AIR P/B must be set to ON. When set to ON, and if DITCHING is not selected, the emergency ram air inlet flap opens.

subtopic: Emergency Ram Air and LP Ground
question: What is the function of the flap installed in the Y-duct between the LP ground connection and the emergency ram air inlet?

options.a: To regulate the pressure of the ground supply
options.b: To close one side of the duct when air is supplied from the other side
options.c: To filter out debris from the ram air

justification: The flap... closes one side of the Y-duct when air is supplied from the other side.

subtopic: Emergency Ram Air and LP Ground
question: For emergency ventilation, at what cabin differential pressure will the CPC half-open the outflow valve?

options.b: At 4 psi
options.c: When the aircraft is on the ground

justification: When the cabin differential pressure is less than 1 psi, the Cabin Pressure Controller... opens the outflow valve. The air then goes through the check valve to the mixing unit.

question: Which controller is responsible for operating the cargo isolation valves and extraction fan?

options.b: The Cargo Ventilation Controller (VC)
options.c: The AEVC

justification: The operation of the two isolation valves and the extract fan is controlled automatically by the cargo Ventilation Controller (VC).

question: From where is air supplied to the cargo compartments for ventilation?

options.a: Directly from the air conditioning packs
options.b: From the main cabin zones
options.c: From a dedicated external air inlet

justification: Air from the main cabin is supplied into the cargo compartment by the extract fan or by differential pressure.

question: How is the temperature increased in a heated cargo compartment?

options.a: By electric heater blankets in the floor
options.b: By mixing hot bleed air with the cabin air coming from the main cabin
options.c: By increasing the flow of air from the aft cabin zone

justification: For the heating of the cargo compartment... hot bleed air is mixed with the air coming from the main cabin to increase the temperature.

question: What is the pilot's control range for cargo compartment temperature?

options.c: 15°C to 30°C

justification: The selector temperature range is between 5°C (41°F) and 26°C (79°F), with 16°C (60°F) at the 12 o'clock position.

question: What is the automatic response of the cargo ventilation controller if cargo smoke is detected?

options.a: It increases the extraction fan speed to clear the smoke
options.b: It automatically closes the related isolation valves
options.c: It automatically discharges the fire bottle

justification: In case of cargo smoke detected, the cargo ventilation controller will automatically close the related isolation valves.

question: What specific temperature threshold causes the cargo heating controller to close the hot air PRV for the cargo compartment?
justification: In case of duct temperature above 88°C (190°F), the heating controller controls the cargo hot air PRV to close.

question: In the event of a FWD Cargo Duct Overheat (88°C), what indications will the crew see?

options.a: A red warning on the EWD and the DITCHING light on
options.b: The FAULT light on the HOT AIR P/B and the MASTER CAUTION with aural warning
options.c: Only a class 3 fault in the CFDS

justification: In case a FWD CaRGo DUCT OVerHeaT condition occurs, the FAULT light on the HOT AIR P/B and the MASTER CAUTion come on, and the aural warning sounds.

question: Why is it important to repair damage to the cargo compartment liner immediately?

options.a: To prevent air leaks into the cabin
options.b: To prevent unwanted airflow through the compartment which could compromise fire protection
options.c: To ensure the isolation valves can be manually locked

justification: A hole in the liner could induce airflow through the compartment, compromising the fire protection... if the compartment is not ventilated, no airflow is permitted.

question: What is indicated by the FAULT light on the FWD ISOLation VALVE P/B?

options.b: A cargo inlet or outlet isolation valve disagrees with the selected position
options.c: The cargo heating controller has failed

justification: When the cargo inlet or outlet isolation valve disagrees with the selected position... the FAULT light on the FWD ISOLation VALVE P/B comes on.

question: What is the critical safety warning regarding the lubrication of oxygen line connectors?

options.b: Never use standard oil (risk of explosion); use only specifically approved lubricants
options.c: Apply standard oil only to the outer sleeve of the connector

justification: The manual states: WARNING: NEVER USE STANDARD OIL TO LUBRICATE THE CONNECTOR THREAD (risk of explosion). ONLY LUBRICANTS... SPECIFICALLY APPROVED FOR OXYGEN must be used.

question: How many wrenches must be used when disconnecting or reconnecting an oxygen line connector, and why?

options.a: One wrench is sufficient if the mounting bracket is secure
options.b: Two wrenches: one for the nut and one for the counter nut to avoid force on the material
options.c: None, they are hand-tightening quick-disconnects

justification: During disconnection/reconnection... use two wrenches: one for the nut and one for the counter nut to avoid force onto the material (risk of rupture and leakage).

question: How often should the APU auto extinguishing test be performed?

options.b: Every 3000 flight hours
options.c: Only after an APU fire detection loop replacement

justification: The APU auto extinguishing test should be performed every 3000 flight hours.

question: Which relay is energized during the APU auto extinguishing test to prevent the fire bottle from discharging?

options.b: The Extinguishing Ground Test Relay (36WF)
options.c: The Relay Auto Push (34WF)

justification: The Extinguishing Ground Test Relay (36WF) is energized to isolate the Fire Extinguishing Bottle... to prevent 28VDC power supply to the filaments... during the Test.

question: What happens when the 'RESET' pushbutton is pressed on the APU AUTO EXTING section of the overhead panel?

options.a: It clears the APU fire warning only
options.b: All relays are de-energized, the bottle is reconnected to the circuit, and lights/horns go off
options.c: It resets the CIDS-SDF function to normal monitoring

justification: When the RESET P/BSW is pressed all the relays are de-energized. The fire bottle is connected to the automatic fire extinguishing circuit again. The horn and the APU FIRE light go off.

question: What is the function of the D-ULPA filter in the IGGS?

options.a: To separate nitrogen from the air stream
options.b: To keep the ASM inlet clean, without hydrocarbons and dust
options.c: To filter the fuel before it enters the center tank

justification: The bleed air comes from the CSAS and it is filtered by the D-ULPA filter to keep the ASM inlet clean, without hydrocarbons and dust.

question: What is the primary purpose of the oxygen sensor located at the outlet of the Air Separation Module (ASM)?

options.a: To measure the temperature of the Nitrogen Enriched Air (NEA)
options.b: To measure the oxygen rate and prevent high oxygen concentration in the center tank
options.c: To calculate the fuel level in the center tank

justification: The oxygen sensor measures the oxygen rate to prevent a high oxygen concentration in the center tank and also has pressure sensing capability.

question: Which component manages the system change between low, middle, and high Nitrogen Enriched Air (NEA) flow?

options.b: The Dual Flow Shut Off Valve (DFSOV)
options.c: The D-ULPA Filter

justification: The DFSOV controls the NEA flow to the fuel tank and lets the system change between low/mid/high NEA flow in relation to flight phases.

question: How does the ASM separate the conditioned air into Nitrogen Enriched Air (NEA) and Oxygen Enriched Air (OEA)?

options.b: Using a semi-permeable hollow-fiber membrane bundle
options.c: Through a series of high-speed centrifugal separators

justification: An ASM is a semi-permeable hollow-fiber membrane bundle contained in a pressure containment canister that divides the air stream.

question: Which unit enables communication between the IGGS controller, the CFDIU, and the FWS?

options.b: The Conditioned Service Air System Controller Unit (CCU)
options.c: The SDAC

justification: The CCU (Conditioned service air system Controller Unit) makes communication possible between the IGGS controller, the CFDIU, and the FWS.

question: What is the function of the temperature and pressure sensors located downstream of the D-ULPA filter?

options.a: They provide data to the cockpit EWD only
options.b: They send air parameters to the IGGS Controller Unit (ICU) for system control
options.c: They regulate the bypass valve directly

justification: Downstream of the D-ULPA filter, one temperature sensor and one pressure sensor send air parameters to the ICU.

question: What happens if the IGGS Controller Unit (ICU) detects an oxygen rate higher than 12% at the ASM outlet?

options.a: It increases the flow rate to high NEA flow
options.b: It de-energizes the IGGS Isolation Gate Valve and the DFSOV solenoids to close the valves
options.c: It triggers a red MASTER WARN on the glareshield

justification: If the oxygen sensor senses an oxygen rate higher than 12%, the ICU de-energizes the IGGS Isolation Gate Valve solenoid and the DFSOV solenoid to close both valves.

question: Under what condition will the ICU automatically close the IGGS Isolation Gate Valve?

options.a: Whenever the center tank fuel level is low
options.b: In case of overpressure or overtemperature air coming from the heat exchanger
options.c: Only when the aircraft is in the descent phase

justification: If there is overpressure or overtemperature, the ICU de-energizes the IGGS Isolation Gate Valve solenoid to close the valve.

question: What logic does the CCU follow if the CSAS stops due to an overtemperature scenario?

options.a: It automatically switches to Engine 2 as a source
options.b: It informs the ICU that the system is closed and they compare sensor readings from both systems
options.c: It overrides the ICU and forces the DFSOV to remain open

justification: If the CSAS stops because of overtemperature, the CCU tells the ICU that the system is closed and they compare readings of the sensors from the two systems.

question: Besides oxygen rate, what other sensing capability is integrated into the oxygen sensor?

options.b: Pressure sensing
options.c: Flow rate calculation

justification: The oxygen sensor has a pressure sensing capability when it is energized and thus it prevents over-pressure in the center tank.

question: What is the default state of the IGGS isolation valve when not energized?

options.b: Spring-loaded closed
options.c: It remains in its last position

justification: The IGGS isolation valve is a solenoid valve. It is spring-loaded closed.

question: What is the standard percentage of oxygen in normal atmospheric air?
justification: The training manual states the air is made of 21% oxygen, 78% nitrogen and 1% other gases.

question: Which physical property makes gaseous oxygen particularly dangerous in low-lying areas?

options.a: It is lighter than air and dissipates quickly
options.b: It is heavier than air and can accumulate in low-lying areas
options.c: It has a distinct smell that can cause nausea

justification: The gaseous oxygen is heavier than air and can accumulate in low lying areas.

question: What oxygen percentage defines an 'oxygen-enriched atmosphere'?

options.b: 24% and above
options.c: 50% and above

justification: An atmosphere is considered as an oxygen-enriched atmosphere when the oxygen percentage is 24% and above.

question: How does a fire in an oxygen-enriched atmosphere compare to a fire in normal air?

options.a: It is lower in temperature and slower to spread
options.b: It is higher in intensity, temperature, and thermal power
options.c: It produces significantly more smoke but less heat

justification: In comparison to a fire in the air, a fire in an oxygen-enriched atmosphere will be characterized by: high in intensity, higher in temperature and higher in thermal power.

question: What components form the 'Fire Triangle' required for a fire to start?

options.b: Oxygen, Combustible material, and an Ignition source
options.c: Heat, Pressure, and Hydrocarbons

justification: The fire triangle consists of Oxygen, Combustible material and an ignition source. If one is missing, no fire can occur.

question: According to safety precautions, what is the minimum distance that all maintenance procedures must be kept from the oxygen working area?
justification: Prevent all maintenance procedures nearer than 5m (16.4ft) from the working area of the aircraft.

question: Why must a person who has been in an oxygen-filled area avoid ignition sources for at least 15 minutes?

options.a: Because oxygen affects the person's nervous system
options.b: Because clothes and hair tend to absorb oxygen and keep a high concentration for some time
options.c: Because pure oxygen causes static electricity to build up on skin

justification: Clothes and hair tend to absorb oxygen... This oxygen stays on for some time. This person must avoid any source of ignition for 15 minutes.

question: What is a potential cause of 'oxygen overheating' during system operation?

options.b: Sudden pressurization due to quick opening or closure of oxygen valves
options.c: Storing the bottles in the L/H avionics compartment

justification: Ignition sources include oxygen overheating due to quick opening or closure of oxygen valves (sudden pressurization).

question: What is the danger if an oxygen cylinder head valve breaks off?

options.a: The cylinder will simply vent slowly and safely
options.b: The high-pressure cylinder becomes an unguided missile
options.c: The oxygen will immediately freeze the surrounding structure

justification: High pressure is potentially dangerous... if a valve brakes off a high-pressure cylinder, the container becomes an unguided missile.

question: What must be done if a thunderstorm occurs during oxygen filling operations?

options.a: Continue filling but ensure the aircraft is grounded
options.b: Immediately stop all oxygen filling operations
options.c: Switch the filling equipment to battery power

justification: If a thunderstorm can occur, immediately stop all oxygen filling operations.

question: What is the function of the Portable Breathing Equipment (PBE)?

options.a: To provide therapeutic oxygen to passengers
options.b: To provide eye protection and oxygen to crew members to allow freedom of movement to extinguish a fire
options.c: To backup the flight crew oxygen system if the main cylinder fails

justification: The PBE supplies breathing means and eye protection to flight/cabin crew. It lets them move freely to extinguish a fire.

question: How is the PBE stored to ensure its serviceability?

options.b: Vacuum-packed in a transport/storage container
options.c: Inside the main oxygen cylinder cradle

justification: The PBE is vacuum-packed in a transport/storage container.

question: By what mechanism is oxygen generated within the PBE hood?

options.b: Exothermic chemical reaction between potassium peroxide (KO2) and expired air (humidity/CO2)
options.c: Compressed oxygen from a small attached 1850 psi cylinder

justification: The oxygen is generated in exothermic chemical reaction between the potassium peroxide (KO2), the humidity, and the carbon dioxide (CO2) in the expired air.

question: What is the function of the anti-suffocation valve in the PBE inner mask?

options.a: To allow the user to breathe if the chemical reaction stops
options.b: To allow the user to inhale from the volume between head and hood if breathing resistance is high
options.c: To vent excess heat from the KO2 reaction

justification: The inner mask is installed with an anti-suffocation valve... The user can inhale through this valve from the volume between head and hood.

question: What physical indication confirms a PBE is unserviceable after the box has been opened?

options.b: The serviceability indicator is broken
options.c: The phonic membrane is missing

justification: The serviceability indicator is broken after opening the box.

question: What is the minimum autonomy duration provided by the Portable Breathing Equipment (PBE)?

options.b: 20 minutes
options.c: 30 minutes

justification: The diagram on page 545 clearly labels 'MINIMUM AUTONOMY OF THE PORTABLE BREATHING EQUIPMENT: 20 min.'

question: Which PBE indicator color typically shows a 'good condition' state before opening the container?

options.b: Green or Yellow (depending on supplier)
options.c: Blue

justification: The manual mentions: 'e.g. green - operational' and 'another indicator is available which shows a yellow indicator if the container has not been opened.'

question: What starts the oxygen generation cycle in the PBE once the box is opened?

options.b: Activating a starter via a lanyard
options.c: Closing the neck seal

justification: The system is activated by a starter via a lanyard.

question: To provide therapeutic oxygen to passengers, what type of mask is used with the high-pressure portable cylinder?

options.b: Continuous-flow type mask
options.c: Full-face pressure mask

justification: The high-pressure portable cylinder includes continuous-flow type masks and supplies first aid oxygen to the passengers.

question: What is the capacity of the cabin portable oxygen bottle shown in the manual?

options.b: 310 Liters (11 cubic feet)
options.c: 115 cubic feet

justification: The diagram on page 547 states 'OXYGEN BOTTLE CAPACITY: 310 l (11 ft3)'.

question: Which units provide digital inputs via ARINC 429 buses to the Bleed Monitoring Computer (BMC)?

options.a: The opposite BMC, corresponding Engine Interface Unit (EIU), and CFDIU
options.b: The Flight Management Computer only
options.c: The Landing Gear Control and Interface Unit

justification: Each BMC has digital inputs from the opposite BMC, corresponding EIU, and CFDIU.

question: Which system receives discrete outputs from the BMC for APU availability monitoring?

options.b: The APU Electronic Control Box (ECB)
options.c: The Flight Warning Computer (FWC)

justification: Each BMC has discrete outputs to the APU Electronic Control Box (ECB) for APU availability.

question: What information is exchanged between the two BMCs via the crosstalk bus?

options.b: Wing loop leak status and bleed parameters
options.c: Cabin temperature setpoints

justification: BMCs exchange data via an ARINC bus for wing double loop detection (Wing loop leak status and bleed parameters).

question: Which BMC unit is specifically responsible for sending APU BLEED FAULT signals to the overhead panel?

options.b: BMC 2 only
options.c: Both BMCs provide redundant signals

justification: The discrete output for APU BLEED FAULT is from BMC 1 ONLY.

question: Which component receives discrete outputs from the BMC to control the bleed PRVs?

options.b: The control solenoid for PRV control
options.c: The high pressure valve

justification: BMCs provide discrete outputs to the CTL SOLENOID FOR PRV CTL.

question: In the event of a total BMC failure, what happens to the control and monitoring of the engine bleed system?

options.a: All monitoring and control is completely lost
options.b: Monitoring of main parameters is kept, but automatic control of the PRV is lost
options.c: The opposite BMC takes over all functions including automatic valve control

justification: In case of BMC failure, the monitoring of main parameters... is kept, but the automatic control of the PRV is lost.

question: Does the BMC BITE (Built-In Test Equipment) confirm the pneumatic integrity of the system?

options.a: Yes, it performs a pressure leak test during power-up
options.b: No, the BMC BITE does not confirm the integrity of the system
options.c: Only if the aircraft is in flight configuration

justification: The Troubleshooting Note on page 45 states: The BMC BITE does not confirm the integrity of the system.

question: What is the purpose of the 'Test Set' available for pneumatic system troubleshooting?

options.b: To apply calibrated pressure to individual valves and sense lines to check for operation and integrity
options.c: To manually override the engine FADEC limits

justification: A Test Set... enables calibrated pressure to be applied to individual valves, components and isolated parts of the system to check for normal operation and sense line integrity.

question: What maintenance check is considered 'very important' during pneumatic system troubleshooting?

options.a: Checking the oil level in the PRV
options.b: Checking the integrity of all pneumatic sense-line connections between valves and thermostats/solenoids
options.c: Replacing the BMC after every 500 flight hours

justification: During troubleshooting, it is very important to check the integrity of all pneumatic sense-line connections, in between the valves and its thermostat or solenoid.

question: Which unit receives digital outputs from the BMC to generate ECAM warnings and indications?

options.b: System Data Acquisition Concentrator (SDAC)
options.c: Engine Interface Unit (EIU)

justification: BMCs send digital outputs via ARINC 429 to the System Data Acquisition Concentrators (SDACs) for ECAM warnings and indications.

question: How many fire detection loops are provided for the APU?

options.b: Two identical detection loops (A and B)
options.c: Three loops: pylon, core, and fan

justification: The engines and the APU have individual fire detection systems. Each system has two identical detection loops (A and B) installed in parallel.

question: How many fire extinguisher bottles are installed for the APU?

options.b: Two bottles
options.c: The APU uses the Engine 2 bottles as backup

justification: For the APU, there is only one fire extinguisher bottle, which is installed in the aft fuselage forward of the APU firewall.

question: What causes the APU fire extinguisher bottle to discharge automatically on the ground?

options.a: Only when the pilot releases the APU FIRE pushbutton
options.b: Detection of an APU fire on ground
options.c: Whenever the APU EGT exceeds 700°C

justification: When an APU fire is detected on ground, the APU shuts down automatically and the fire extinguishing system is automatically triggered.

question: Which APU fire detection loop is capable of triggering automatic extinguishing on the ground?

options.b: APU Fire Loop 'A' only
options.c: Both loops must agree for automatic discharge

justification: The manual states: NOTE: APU automatic extinguishing is only triggered by APU Fire Loop 'A'.

question: In the event of an APU fire in flight, which unit receives a signal to initiate an emergency shutdown?

options.b: The APU Electronic Control Box (ECB)
options.c: The FADEC

justification: Releasing the APU FIRE P/BSW triggers the ECB to initiate an emergency APU shutdown.

question: How can the pilot verify that APU fire bottle percussion is available (armed) after a fire is detected?

options.a: By checking the pressure gage on the bottle
options.b: The SQUIB light illuminates on the AGENT P/BSW
options.c: The DISCH light illuminates immediately

justification: The SQUIB light comes on to indicate that the fire bottle can be used after the FIRE pushbutton is released out.

question: After an APU fire is detected in flight and isolated, why is a 10-second delay required before discharging the agent?

options.a: To allow the APU to spool down completely
options.b: To allow the airflow in the compartment to reduce, increasing the agent effect
options.c: To wait for the 'AVAIL' light to go out

justification: A 10 s delay allows the airflow to reduce, this increases the agent effect.

question: On the ground, what external indications are provided during an APU fire?

options.a: The red MASTER WARN light only
options.b: The APU FIRE light on the External Power panel illuminates and the external horn sounds
options.c: The APU EGT gauge flashes red

justification: When fire is detected on ground... The APU FIRE light on the EXTernal PoWeR panel comes on, and the external horn sounds.

question: During an APU auto extinguishing test on ground, which relay prevents the 28VDC power from reaching the fire bottle squibs?

options.b: The Extinguishing Ground Test Relay (36WF)
options.c: The Fire EMER Stop Relay (5WF)

justification: The 36WF relay opens to interrupt power supply to the filaments of the Fire Extinguishing Bottle Cartridge during the test.

question: Is it necessary to use the APU SHUT OFF switch on the External Power panel if the auto extinguishing system has already operated?

options.b: No, it is not necessary in case of APU fire auto extinguishing
options.c: Only if the external horn continues to sound

justification: The manual states: NOTE: It is not necessary to use the APU SHUT OFF switch on the EXT PWR panel in case of APU fire auto extinguishing.

question: What is the purpose of the manual ON/OFF valve on the crew oxygen cylinder?

options.a: To regulate the flow to the masks in flight
options.b: To isolate the cylinder for maintenance purposes
options.c: To manually drop the passenger masks in an emergency

justification: This cylinder can be isolated for maintenance by a manual ON/OFF valve.

question: Where is the direct-reading pressure gage for the crew oxygen cylinder located?

options.b: Directly on the cylinder head assembly
options.c: On the external refueling panel

justification: A direct-reading pressure gage (on the cylinder head) gives an indication of the cylinder pressure.

question: What is the standard storage pressure for a crew oxygen cylinder at 21°C?

options.c: 2500 psi

justification: The flight crew oxygen is supplied from a high-pressure oxygen cylinder at a pressure of 127.5 bar (1.850 psig).

question: At what pressure does the low-pressure safety relief valve set the limit for the distribution system?

options.b: 175 psig
options.c: 400 psig

justification: The pressure relief valve sets the limit of the low-pressure oxygen supply to 175 psig.

question: How is the high-pressure safety outlet constructed on the cylinder?

options.b: As a frangible disk type that ruptures at excessive pressure
options.c: As a manual vent screw

justification: The high-pressure safety outlet is a frangible disk type... Rupture of the frangible disk is set at a cylinder pressure of 2500 to 2775 psig.

question: What is the first step in the 'Job Set-up' for removing the crew oxygen cylinder?

options.b: Close the valve of the oxygen cylinder valve assembly
options.c: Bleed the oxygen system by actuating a mask

justification: The setup procedure starts with: Close the valve of the oxygen cylinder valve assembly.

question: What must be done to the union after disconnecting the pressure regulator during cylinder removal?

options.b: Discard the bush and install a blanking cap
options.c: Lubricate the threads with standard oil

justification: Disconnect the union and discard the bush. Put a blanking cap on the union.

question: During the leak test after installation, how far should the cylinder valve be opened initially?

options.b: 3.5 to 4 turns, very slowly
options.c: Exactly one half turn

justification: Very slowly, open the valve of the cylinder 3.5 to 4 turns. Let the pressure become stable.

question: How long must you wait for pressure stabilization before performing the final leak check on the oxygen connections?

options.b: 90 seconds
options.c: 5 minutes

justification: Let the pressure become stable, this occurs after approximately 90 seconds.

question: What is the purpose of the fluorescent yellow reflective area on the overboard discharge indicator?

options.a: To help locate the aircraft at night
options.b: It shows when the green disk is blown out, indicating cylinder discharge or relief valve operation
options.c: It indicates the system is in 'TEST' mode

justification: If there is overpressure... a yellow indicator comes into view to show that the cylinder was discharged or the pressure relief valve is open.

question: Which cockpit indication confirms that smoke has been detected in the avionics equipment?

options.a: APU BLEED FAULT light on the overhead
options.b: MASTER CAUTION, Single Chime, and GEN 1 LINE SMOKE light
options.c: A red 'AVIONICS FIRE' message on the EWD

justification: When smoke is detected, the MASTER CAUTion comes on, the Single Chime (SC) sounds, GENerator 1 LINE SMOKE light comes on.

question: Why is the BLOWER fan stopped by selecting OVRD during an avionics smoke condition?

options.a: To allow the crew to breathe without noise interference
options.b: To stop blowing smoke into the equipment and switch the system to use AC packs as a cold air source
options.c: To prevent the electrical fire from spreading to the cargo compartment

justification: When the BLOWER P/BSW is set to OVRD, the blower fan stops and the air conditioning system is used as a cold air source by opening the air conditioning inlet valve.

question: How is smoke evacuated overboard during the smoke procedure?

options.b: Through the auxiliary flap of the Skin Air Outlet Valve
options.c: Through the emergency ram air inlet

justification: The air is extracted overboard through the auxiliary flap inside the Skin Air Outlet Valve, which is partially open.

question: Which bus remains supplied when the aircraft is in emergency electrical configuration during a smoke procedure?

options.b: AC ESS BUS
options.c: DC BUS 2

justification: The emergency electrical network (AC ESS BUS) is supplied by the emergency generator (EMER GEN).

question: What is the consequence for the ECAM displays when the 'GEN 2' PB is set to OFF during the emergency configuration sequence?

options.a: Both displays remain supplied by the EMER GEN
options.b: The lower ECAM display is no longer supplied
options.c: The upper ECAM display is lost

justification: As both engine generators have been disconnected... the lower ECAM display is no longer supplied.

question: Which engine generator must be kept running during the initial stages of smoke source isolation to ensure fuel pump operation?

options.b: Engine 2
options.c: The APU Generator

justification: With the emergency generator running... Engine 1 generator must be kept running for fuel pump operation.

question: What action is required if smoke persists after 5 minutes of ventilation system reconfiguration?

options.b: Isolating the electrical smoke source by following EWD actions
options.c: Resetting the AEVC

justification: As smoke is still perceptible, it is necessary to act on the electrical system. The actions shown on the EWD indicate how to shed the normal electrical network.

question: Which unit is used to extend the Ram Air Turbine (RAT) manually during the smoke procedure?

options.b: The EMER ELEC PWR MANual ON PB
options.c: The RAT DISCH PB on the maintenance panel

justification: The MANual ON P/B (on the EMER ELEC PWR panel) must be selected to extend the Ram Air Turbine (RAT).

question: Where are the emergency generator parameters displayed for the crew?

options.b: On the ECAM
options.c: On a dedicated gage in the electronics rack

justification: The emergency generator parameters are displayed on the ECAM.

question: What does the ETOPS rule require for cargo hold protection duration?

options.b: Diversion time (e.g. 120 or 180 min) plus 15 minutes supplemental
options.c: Total flight time plus 1 hour

justification: The ETOPS rules require the A/C to be protected... for the duration of the diversion (120 min, 180 min) with added 15 min supplemental.

question: What additional feature is installed on the second cargo fire bottle for ETOPS configurations?

options.b: A flow metering system
options.c: A manual hand-pump interface

justification: Such features with the dual shot system configuration, requires: an additional bottle... a flow metering system on the second bottle.

question: What are the components of the ETOPS flow metering system?

options.a: Two high-pressure pumps and a timer
options.b: Water and solid particle filters, a pressure reducer, and a diaphragm
options.c: An electrical heater and a variable orifice valve

justification: This ETOPS flow metering system is made of: a water absorbing filter, a solid particle filter, a pressure reducer, a diaphragm (for flow metering) and non-return valve.

question: What is the timing for the discharge of the second bottle on an ETOPS aircraft?

options.b: 60 minutes after the first bottle
options.c: Only if smoke is detected after 30 minutes

justification: NOTE: the second bottle on ETOPS A/C will be discharged through a flow metering system 60 min. after the first bottle.

question: Which panel is used in ETOPS configurations to control the discharge of the second cargo fire bottle?

options.b: The optional dual shot CARGO SMOKE panel (22VU)
options.c: The maintenance panel (50VU)

justification: This optional panel 22VU has an additional feature to control the discharge on the second cargo fire bottle... also called dual shot system.

question: What prevents the second cargo fire bottle from being discharged before the first bottle?

options.a: A mechanical interlock on the pushbuttons
options.b: A priority relay
options.c: The CIDS-SDF software logic only

justification: A priority relay prevents the bottle 2 to be discharged before bottle 1.

question: In the A318, A319, and A320 ETOPS 180 min configuration, what is the size of the two extinguisher bottles?

options.b: 630 cubic inches
options.c: 1500 cubic inches

justification: For the A318, A319 and the A320, two 630 cu. in. bottles to protect up to 180 min ETOPS.

question: Where is the ETOPS bottle and flow metering system installed on an A319CJ to account for maintenance access constraints?

options.b: On the side or AFT of the bulk cargo hold
options.c: Inside the landing gear bay

justification: Particularly with the installation of the ACT on the A319CJ... such bottles, squib and flow metering system are installed on the side or AFT of the bulk cargo hold.

question: Which lights illuminate on the 22VU panel when the TEST pushbutton is pressed in an ETOPS configuration?

options.a: SMOKE and DISCH lights (both FWD and AFT)
options.b: The MASTER WARN and MASTER CAUT lights only
options.c: The AGENT 1 and AGENT 2 SQUIB lights

justification: Indications appear on the cargo smoke panel 22VU as follows: the FWD and AFT smoke indication lights come on, the FWD and AFT discharge indication lights come on.

question: What is the consequence of a single CIDS director failure regarding the cargo smoke detection function?

options.b: The function is transferred to the remaining SDF card in the other director
options.c: The system automatically discharges the fire bottles

justification: If one SDF card in one CIDS director fails, the smoke detection function is transferred to the remaining SDF card in the other CIDS director.

question: Where is the oxygen fill panel located on the aircraft?

options.b: Behind the access door on the lower fuselage forward area
options.c: In the aft cargo compartment

justification: The diagram on page 437 shows the ACCESS DOOR for the oxygen filling port on the lower fuselage forward area.

question: What must be used to calculate the correct filling pressure for oxygen cylinders?

options.a: The aircraft placards and the outside/cargo temperatures
options.b: A standard value of 2500 psi regardless of temperature
options.c: The remaining pressure shown on the ECAM only

justification: The correct filling pressure depends on the outside and the cargo compartment temperatures, and can be determined by the use of the aircraft placards.

question: What is the function of the thermal compensator during oxygen replenishment?

options.a: To heat the oxygen to prevent freezing
options.b: To limit the increase in temperature in each cylinder during filling
options.c: To stabilize the pressure transducer readings

justification: During filling, an increase in temperature in each cylinder is limited by a thermal compensator.

question: What safety feature is integrated into the oxygen filling port to ensure a safe pressure rise?

options.b: A flow restrictor
options.c: A remote-controlled shut-off solenoid

justification: The oxygen filling port has: a flow restrictor to make sure safe pressure rises.

question: Why must the aircraft be electrostatically grounded during oxygen servicing?

options.a: To ensure the ECAM gauges are accurate
options.b: To prevent static discharge which could act as an ignition source
options.c: To provide power to the charging equipment

justification: Ignition sources include electrical discharge (static electricity). Procedure states: Electrostatically ground the aircraft and also electrostatically bond the oxygen charging equipment.

question: How should the hand-valves of the oxygen cylinder be operated for flight?

options.a: Closed for safety, then opened in flight by the crew
options.b: Opened very slowly and turned to the fully open position
options.c: Opened exactly 3.5 turns and then safety-wired

justification: Open the hand-valves of the oxygen cylinder very slowly and turn them to the fully open position.

question: What is the consequence of not fully opening the oxygen cylinder hand-valves before flight?

options.a: The masks will not drop automatically
options.b: The oxygen pressure data on the ECAM page will not be correct
options.c: The pressure relief valve will blow out

justification: In the case the hand-valves are not fully open before flight, the data of the oxygen pressure on the corresponding ECAM page will not be correct.

question: What must be installed on the air data probes when the aircraft is parked to protect from contamination?

options.b: Protective covers marked with 'REMOVE BEFORE FLIGHT'
options.c: Static discharge wicks

justification: When the aircraft is parked, it is recommended to install protective covers on the air data probes... marked with REMOVE BEFORE FLIGHT.

question: Can oxygen be used for other purposes, such as tire inflation?

options.b: No, never use oxygen for other purposes such as tire or accumulator inflation
options.c: Only for blowing dust from electronics

justification: Oxygen must be used only for oxygen system servicing. Never use oxygen for other purposes such as tire or accumulator inflation, blowing of dust...

question: What should be done if the oxygen pressures in each cylinder do not increase smoothly and at the same time during filling?

options.b: Stop the filling procedure immediately
options.c: Continue filling until all cylinders equalize

justification: Stop the filling procedure immediately if the pressures in each oxygen cylinder do not increase smoothly and at the same time.

question: What manual should be consulted if a pneumatic fault symptom is identified?

options.b: The Trouble Shooting Manual (TSM)
options.c: The Flight Crew Operating Manual (FCOM)

justification: The maintenance tips include an example of a troubleshooting task from the TSM (Trouble Shooting Manual).

question: Where are the primary components of the pneumatic system installed?

options.b: On the engines and in the pylons
options.c: In the main landing gear bay

justification: The primary components of the pneumatic system are installed on the engines and in the pylons.

question: What is the purpose of the sensing lines in the pneumatic system?

options.a: To supply lubrication to the valves
options.b: To provide reference pressure to thermostats or solenoids for valve control
options.c: To drain moisture from the precooler

justification: The HPV, PRV, OPV and FAV are connected to a dedicated reference pressure pneumatic Thermostat or solenoid through sense lines.

question: Is electric power required for the normal operation of the pneumatic system valves (HPV, PRV, OPV, FAV)?

options.a: Yes, they are all electrically driven
options.b: No, they are all controlled and operated pneumatically
options.c: Only for the Overpressure Valve (OPV)

justification: Normal operation of the pneumatic system does not require electric power. The HPV, PRV, OPV and FAV are all controlled and operated pneumatically.

question: What indicates the transferred pressure downstream from the High Pressure Valve (HPV)?

options.b: A transducer connected to the related BMC
options.c: A mechanical gage on the engine core

justification: A transducer, connected to the related BMC, reads the transferred pressure downstream from the High Pressure Valve (HPV).

question: What is the first step in troubleshooting a Fan Air Valve (FAV) fault according to the TSM example?

options.b: Check the unions and clamps of the sense line between the FAV control thermostat and the FAV
options.c: Replace the precooler

justification: The TSM example on page 46 says: 'do a check of the unions and clamps of the sense line between the fan air valve control thermostat and the fan air valve.'

question: If the unions on a pneumatic sense line are correctly tightened but a fault persists, what should be checked next?

options.b: The filter of the control thermostat
options.c: The crossbleed valve electrical connector

justification: According to the TSM flow: '(2) If the unions are correctly tightened: do a check of the filter of the fan air valve control thermostat.'

question: When using the pneumatic test set, what is the required pressure to check for full opening of the Fan Air Valve (FAV)?

options.c: 44 psi

justification: The TSM example states: 'slowly apply 20 psi (1.3789 bar) at its test port... The visual indicator must show that the fan air valve is fully open.'

question: Which maintenance message is generated if the precooler exchanger outlet temperature reaches 240°C?

options.b: AIR BLEED
options.c: PRECOOLER FAULT

justification: If the precooler exchanger outlet temperature reaches 240°C (464°F), the BMC generates a class 2 maintenance message - 'AIR BLEED' - on the ECAM STATUS page.

question: When deactivating a PRV or HPV, what must be done to the thrust reverser for safety?

options.a: Fully deploy it to gain access
options.b: Deactivate the thrust reverser at the Hydraulic Control Unit (HCU)
options.c: Remove the thrust reverser translating sleeve

justification: The deactivation procedure includes: 'deactivate the thrust reverser at the Hydraulic Control Unit (HCU)'.

question: Which computer sends data to the ACSC for altitude compensation during zone and pack temperature control?

options.b: The Cabin Pressure Controller (CPC)
options.c: The ADIRU

justification: The Cabin Pressure Controller (CPC) 1 or 2... sends data to the ACSC for zone and pack temperature control.

question: Which unit receives the 'APU flow increase' signal from the ACSC?

options.b: The APU Electronic Control Box (ECB)
options.c: The CFDIU

justification: The ACSC... sends to the ECB the increase of APU flow used for increased bleed airflow.

question: How do the ACSCs receive signals from the recirculation and toilet fans for monitoring?

options.b: As discrete signals
options.c: Through the CIDS Directors only

justification: The ACSCs receive discrete signals from recirculation and toilet fans for monitoring.

question: What is the purpose of the 'ground/flight' signal sent from LGCIU 2 to the ACSCs?

options.a: To control the cabin temperature setpoint
options.b: For pack ram air inlet flap closure during take-off and landing phases
options.c: To toggle the master CPC

justification: Landing Gear Control and Interface Unit (LGCIU) 2 sends a ground/flight signal... used for pack ram air inlet flap closure during take-off and landing phases.

question: Which information is sent from the ACSC to the Flight Data Interface and Management Unit (FDIMU) for maintenance?

options.a: Trim-air PRV position, pack flow, and temperatures
options.b: Only the cabin pressure values
options.c: Passenger address volume levels

justification: The ACSC sends to the FDIMU: the trim-air Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV) position, pack flow, water extractor and pack compressor discharge temperatures, BYPass valve and ram air inlet flap positions.

question: How much can the Flight Attendant Panel (FAP) adjust the temperature in the cabin zones?
justification: The CIDS Director 1 (or 2) sends a signal... for temperature regulation (+ or - 2.5°C) from the Flight Attendant Panel (FAP).

question: What occurs automatically if the DITCHING pushbutton is pressed?

options.b: The ACSCs close both pack flow control valves
options.c: The safety valves open to depressurize the aircraft

justification: The ACSCs also receive a signal from the DITCHING P/B to close both pack FCVs if there is a ditching.

question: Which unit sends a 'wheel signal' used for pack ram air inlet flap closure during takeoff and landing?

options.b: The Braking/Steering Control Unit (BSCU)
options.c: The ADIRU

justification: The Braking/Steering Control Unit (BSCU) sends a wheel signal to both ACSCs... used for pack ram air inlet flap closure during take-off and landing phases.

question: If an engine FIRE pushbutton is released out, what is the effect on the associated pack?

options.a: The pack switches to high flow to clear smoke
options.b: The related pack FCV is closed automatically
options.c: The pack bypass valve is driven fully open

justification: ACSC 1 and 2 receive a signal from the engine FIRE P/B, to close the related pack FCV in case of engine fire.

question: What data is used by the EIUs for thrust limit calculation received from the air conditioning system?

options.b: The bleed and the anti-ice status
options.c: The position of the ram air inlet flaps

justification: The ACSC sends to EIUs 1 and 2... the bleed and the anti-ice status used for thrust limit calculation.

question: Where is the mixer unit installed in the aircraft?

options.b: At the rear of the forward cargo compartment
options.c: Directly in the electronics bay

justification: The mixer unit is installed at the rear of the forward cargo compartment.

question: Which component is used for the catalytic removal of ozone from the hot bleed air?

options.b: The Ozone Converter
options.c: The water extractor

justification: High-pressure, high-temperature air... is supplied... through the OZONE CONVERTER, which is used for catalytic removal of ozone.

question: What is the function of the Water Extractor within the pack?

options.a: To spray water onto the heat exchangers
options.b: To use centrifugal forces to extract water from the cold air stream
options.c: To filter the air entering the cabin

justification: Guide vanes will supply air at high speed and centrifugal forces will extract the water from the air flow.

question: How is the air cooled before it enters the ACM compressor?

options.b: In the primary heat exchanger using external ram air
options.c: By the water injector

justification: The PRIMary HEAT EXCHanGeR is used to decrease the temperature of the hot bleed air before it goes into the ACM compressor.

question: What results from the expansion of air in the ACM turbine section?

options.b: A very low turbine discharge air temperature and air pressure
options.c: A fast increase in air energy through kinetic heating

justification: The air expands in the turbine section, which results in a very low turbine discharge air temperature. The result is a fast decrease of the air pressure and air temperature.

question: What is the function of the mixer unit flap?

options.a: To balance the pressure between the LH and RH packs
options.b: To ensure sufficient fresh air is delivered to the cockpit in case of pack 1 failure
options.c: To vent excess air from the cabin during emergency descents

justification: An electrically operated mixer unit flap is installed to ensure that sufficient fresh air is delivered to the cockpit in case of pack 1 failure.

question: What are the temperature limits signaled by the COMPRESSOR DISCHARGE TEMP SENSOR for pack control?

options.b: 180°C (normal) and 215°C (flow reduction start)
options.c: 450°C for fire shutdown

justification: If the pack compressor outlet temperature is > 215°C (419°F), the FCV starts to reduce the flow. 180°C is mentioned as normal operation.

question: Under what condition does the ACM fan bypass in flight?

options.a: When the aircraft is below 15,000 ft
options.b: Whenever ram air is available to prevent a negative effect on ACM operation
options.c: Only during high-altitude cruise

justification: In flight with ram air available, the fan will be bypassed to prevent a negative effect on the ACM operation.

question: What is the maximum negative temperature that the ACM turbine can produce?
justification: The result is a fast decrease... to below 0°C (-50°C as maximum negative temperature).

question: Which component manages 'long term' pack temperature control?

options.a: The Bypass Valve (BYP VLV) stepper motor
options.b: The RAM AIR ACTUATOR (ram air inlet flap)
options.c: The Pack Flow Control Valve torque motor

justification: For long term pack temperature control, the ACSC modulates the ram air cooling flow through... the RAM AIR ACTUATOR.

question: What action occurs when the flight crew pulls the oxygen mask out of the stowage box?

options.b: A supply valve in the stowage box opens to let oxygen flow to the mask
options.c: The cockpit loudspeaker is automatically disabled

justification: When the mask is pulled out of the box, a supply valve installed in the stowage box opens and lets oxygen flow to the mask.

question: What color is the oxygen flow blinker when oxygen is flowing through the regulator?

options.b: Yellow
options.c: Black

justification: Oxygen flow is indicated by the blinker showing yellow (and goes black again showing that the regulator is leak tight).

question: What is the purpose of the 'reset test slider' on the oxygen mask stowage box?

options.a: To manually release the mask for cleaning
options.b: To retract the OXY ON flag after restowing and to test regulator leak-tightness
options.c: To calibrate the pressure gage on the cylinder

justification: Close the left flap door... while pushing the reset test slider to retract the OXY ON flag. Pushing the slider also shows if the regulator is leak tight.

question: How is the cockpit oxygen mask harness inflated for donning?

options.b: By squeezing the red clips on the mask
options.c: By turning the emergency rotation knob

justification: To use the mask, squeeze the red clips. This will inflate the mask harness.

question: What happens to the oxygen flow in the mask harness when the red clips are released?

options.b: Oxygen flow to the harness stops and the remaining oxygen in the harness vents to the atmosphere
options.c: The harness locks in the inflated position

justification: When the red clips are released, the oxygen flow to the harness stops and the oxygen that remains in the harness is released into the atmosphere.

question: How is the 'on demand' system of the crew oxygen mask tested?

options.a: By breathing heavily into the mask
options.b: By pressing the emergency rotation knob
options.c: By pulling the mask out of the box and waiting 5 seconds

justification: The on demand system is tested by pressing the emergency rotation knob.

question: How is the mask microphone tested during the in-situ test?

options.b: By activating the loudspeakers/interphone and pressing the emergency rotation knob
options.c: By checking for a green light on the RMP

justification: The microphone is tested by activating the loudspeakers, the interphone, and by pressing the emergency rotation knob.

question: What is the critical orientation for stowing the mask assembly in the box?

options.b: Regulator on top
options.c: Mouthpiece facing the rear

justification: Engage the mask assembly with the regulator on top.

question: If you pull the Engine Interface Unit (EIU) power supply circuit breaker on ground, how will the PHC react regarding probe heating?

options.a: It will cut off all heating for safety
options.b: It will sense an 'engine running' condition and heat the probes
options.c: It will report a CFDIU type 1 failure

justification: If the Engine Interface Unit (EIU) power supply C/B is pulled, the PHC will sense an 'engine running' condition and the probes will be heated.

question: What must be ensured regarding the 'OXY/TMR RESET' switch after a passenger oxygen system fault has been cleared on ground?

options.a: Used chemical units replaced, masks stowed, doors latched, and TMR RESET P/B momentarily pressed on maintenance panel
options.b: The switch must be safety-wired in the ON position
options.c: The altitude pressure switch must be replaced

justification: On ground, used chemical oxygen units must be replaced, all masks stowed and oxygen container doors must be latched closed. The system is reset by momentarily pressing the TMR RESET P/B on the maintenance panel.

question: How many optical smoke detectors are located in the AFT/BULK cargo compartment?

options.b: Four detectors located in two cavities
options.c: Six detectors located in three cavities

justification: Four optical smoke detectors are located in two cavities in the ceiling of the AFT/BULK cargo compartment.

question: Which communication bus connects the cargo smoke detectors to the CIDS directors?

options.b: Controller Area Network (CAN) bus
options.c: RS-232 serial link

justification: The cargo smoke detectors are electrically connected to the Cabin Intercommunication Data System (CIDS) directors via Controller Area Network (CAN) buses.

question: What voting logic is used by the CIDS-SDF to generate a cargo smoke warning in a dual-detector cavity?

options.b: 'AND' logic (both detectors must detect smoke)
options.c: 'MAJORITY' logic (3 out of 4 detectors)

justification: A SMOKE warning is generated when both detectors in a cavity detect smoke ('AND' logic).

question: What happens if one cargo smoke detector in a cavity is declared faulty while the second detector remains operational?

options.a: The smoke detection in that cavity is completely disabled
options.b: The system remains operational and can still trigger a warning using the single remaining detector
options.c: The fire bottle automatically discharges in that compartment for safety

justification: If the test shows a normal operation of the second detector, the first is declared faulty... the system continues monitoring with the single detector.

question: To which unit are inoperative cargo smoke detector FAULT messages sent for maintenance?

options.b: The Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU)
options.c: The Engine Interface Unit

justification: The inoperative cargo smoke detector FAULT is sent to: the CFDIU for maintenance purposes.

question: During a cargo smoke test using the TEST pushbutton, how many times should the SMOKE and DISCH lights come on if both CIDS-SDF channels are healthy?

options.b: Twice
options.c: Three times

justification: When the TEST P/B is pressed and held, the SMOKE and DISCH lights... come on twice... in case of a failure of one CIDS-SDF channel the lamps come on only once.

question: What is the secondary consequence of a cargo smoke detection concerning the ventilation system?

options.a: The extraction fan speed increases to maximum
options.b: The cargo ventilation controller closes the isolation valves of the affected compartment
options.c: The cabin recirculation fans are automatically stopped

justification: In case of FWD or AFT/BULK smoke detection... the cargo ventilation controller closes the isolation valves of the affected compartment.

question: Where is the cargo fire extinguishing bottle located for the A318 and A319 models?

options.b: In the Bulk cargo compartment, RH side
options.c: In the main landing gear bay

justification: The standard system includes one extinguishing bottle... in the AFT bulk cargo compartment, RH side, for A318 and A319.

question: What happens when the cargo smoke TEST pushbutton is released?

options.b: The lights go off, isolation valves open, and the extraction fan starts
options.c: The system enters a 5-minute cooldown period

justification: When the TEST P/B is released, the DISCH lights and the SMOKE lights go off. The isolation valves... open and the extraction fan starts.

question: How is a loss of fire bottle pressure in the cargo system signaled?

options.a: By a red warning on the EWD
options.b: By a Single Chime, MASTER CAUT light, and ECAM message
options.c: By an external horn on the ground only

justification: In case of a fire bottle pressure drop... the following warnings are activated in the cockpit: Single Chime (SC), MASTER CAUT light, ECAM message.

question: What is the purpose of the 'MASK MAN ON' pushbutton switch?

options.a: To test the oxygen flow blinkers
options.b: To manually activate the passenger oxygen system and override the altitude pressure switch
options.c: To refill the cylinders from the cockpit

justification: The MASK MAN ON P/BSW allows the crew to activate the oxygen system as a backup and override the altitude pressure switch.

question: Where is the altitude pressure switch for the passenger oxygen system located?

options.b: In the avionics compartment
options.c: In the tail cone near the APU

justification: The altitude switch... is installed in the avionics compartment.

question: At what cabin altitude does the oxygen supply automatically start in the gaseous oxygen system?
justification: The oxygen supply starts automatically at a cabin pressure equivalent to an altitude exceeding 14,000 ft.

question: What occurs during the first 6 to 9 seconds after the Pressure Oxygen Regulators (PORs) are opened?

options.b: The motor driven SOV is fully opened to surge the Main Distribution Line (MDL)
options.c: The oxygen is heated to 60°C

justification: At first the POR integrated motor driven SOV is fully opened for approximately 6-9 seconds to surge the MDL.

question: At what altitude does the oxygen supply stop automatically as the aircraft descends?

options.c: Ground level

justification: The oxygen supply... stops when the cabin pressure drops below a pressure equivalent to 10,000 ft.

question: What is the meaning of a '- -' indication on the Passenger Oxygen Indication Panel (POXIP)?

options.a: System is in normal standby mode
options.b: Fill Pressure is not available, out of range, or QCCU failure (Class 1 failure)
options.c: Cylinders are 50% full

justification: Pressure value indication replaced by '- -' in BLACK / WHITE (class 1 failure). This occurs if pressure transducers or QCCU fail or are out of range.

question: What condition triggers the 'CHECK' light in AMBER on the POXIP?

options.a: When the system is activated in MANUAL mode
options.b: When the Fill Pressure is between 1600 PSI and 200 PSI (or below 200 PSI)
options.c: Whenever a single mask lanyard is pulled

justification: CASE 2: 1600 PSI > Fill Pressure > 200 PSI... CHECK light on in AMBER. CASE 3: Fill Pressure < 200 PSI... CHECK light on in AMBER.

question: What is the 'engine burst area' protection regarding the Main Distribution Lines (MDLs)?

options.a: The MDLs are made of thick steel in that area
options.b: The MDL is split into two lines (one under floor, one in ceiling) which are joined again after the area
options.c: The MDL is completely bypassed during takeoff

justification: At the FR47/51, the MDL is split in two... One line... below the cabin floor... the other line... above the cabin ceiling. The area where the MDLs are doubled is the engine burst area.

question: What happens if a riser line is damaged in the gaseous oxygen system?

options.b: The riser line SOV closes automatically to isolate the leak
options.c: The oxygen flow rate is tripled to compensate

justification: In normal operation, the riser line SOVs are open. If a riser line is damaged, the riser line SOV closes automatically.

question: What is indicated if the 'CYLINDER FAULT' light is on in AMBER on the POXIP?

options.a: Low pressure in the distribution manifold
options.b: One or more hand valves of the passenger oxygen cylinders are closed
options.c: The QCCU has lost electrical power

justification: One or more hand valves... are closed. Flight phase inhibition 3-9 required... CYLINDER FAULT light on in AMBER.

question: What component in the pack provides moisture extraction?

options.b: The Water Extractor
options.c: The primary heat exchanger

justification: The pack includes a water extractor in order to remove water particles from the air entering the turbine.

question: Where are the pack discharge pressure sensors mounted?

options.b: On the bulkhead between the air conditioning bay and the pressurized cabin
options.c: Directly on the ACM compressor casing

justification: The pack discharge pressure sensor is mounted on the bulkhead between the air conditioning bay and the pressurized cabin.

question: What happens if a pack compressor discharge temperature exceeds 260°C?

options.a: The pack switches to backup mode
options.b: A pack overheat warning is triggered
options.c: The bypass valve closes to increase airflow

justification: A compressor outlet temperature > 260°C (500°F) results in a pack overheat warning.

question: How is the air cooled in the 'Main Heat Exchanger' of the pack?

options.b: Using external ram air as a cooling medium
options.c: Using fuel through a liquid-to-air exchanger

justification: Exchangers - Compressor: Bleed air is ducted to the primary heat exchanger... The air is cooled in the main heat exchanger (using external ram air).

question: What is the function of the torque motor in the pack Flow Control Unit (FCU)?

options.a: To drive the ram air actuator
options.b: To modulate the position of the FCV under the control of the ACSC
options.c: To provide mechanical force for turbine startup

justification: The flow regulation is a function of the torque motor controlled by the related ACSC compared with the flow setting on panel 30VU.

question: During single pack operations with a failed FCV secured CLOSED, what are the altitude limits for dispatch?

options.b: Limited to 31,500 / 35,400 / 37,000 ft (depending on aircraft/engine combination)
options.c: No altitude limits, but cabin occupancy is reduced

justification: With the valve secured in the CLOSED position, single pack operations are limited to 31,500 / 35,400 / 37,000 ft.

question: In the MEL deactivation procedure for the pack FCV, what is done with the blanking cap?

options.a: It is discarded and replaced with a new one
options.b: It is removed from position (A) and installed between the forks of the valve position lever and boss (B)
options.c: It is used to cap the sense line only

justification: Procedure: remove the blanking cap from the position (A)... install the blanking cap between the forks of the valve position lever and on screwed boss (B).

question: What happens if a pack outlet temperature exceeds 88°C (190°F)?

options.b: A pack overheat warning is triggered on the ECAM
options.c: The bypass valve opens fully to increase heating

justification: The pack outlet temperature sensor also gives pack overheat warning indications if the pack outlet temperature exceeds 88°C (190°F).

question: Which component does the ACSC 1 and 2 monitor to adjust the engine idle setting during high cooling demand?

options.b: The COMPRESSOR DISCHARGE TEMP SENSOR
options.c: The water extractor temperature sensor

justification: Also, when engines are idle, if the cooling demand cannot be satisfied, the engine idle setting can be changed by a thrust demand... The PACK INLET PRESSURE SENSOR is used to calculate the bleed air necessary.

question: Which valve in the FCU is controlled by 'Solenoid 2' and switches the pack between MAIN and BACK-UP operation?

options.b: The Flow Control Valve (FCV)
options.c: The trim air PRV

justification: Solenoid 2 controls the MAIN or BACK-UP operation... When this solenoid is de-energized, the FCV operates in MAIN mode. The solenoid is energized for BACK-UP.

question: Which indicator light on the overhead panel illuminates when the passenger oxygen system is electrically supplied?

options.b: SYS ON (White)
options.c: PASSENGER FAULT (Amber)

justification: The passenger SYStem ON indicator light comes on white when the passenger oxygen system is electrically supplied.

question: Where is the failure indication for a lavatory smoke detector shown?

options.a: Only on the FWC test page
options.b: In the cockpit and on the Flight Attendant Panel (FAP)
options.c: On the external refueling panel

justification: The lavatory detection fault is shown in the cockpit and on the FAP for the cabin.

question: How is a loss of electrical power to a passenger oxygen regulator indicated on the POXIP?

options.b: The REGUL SYS 1 and/or REGUL SYS 2 light illuminates in AMBER
options.c: The pressure readout drops to 0

justification: One or both pressure regulators have a power loss: REGUL SYS1 and/or REGUL SYS2 light on in AMBER.

question: In manual mode, what provides the cabin altitude indication data to the Electronic Instrumentation System (EIS)?

options.b: The ADIRUs and the SDAC
options.c: The CPC 2 backup channel

justification: If the MAN Part of CPC1 is active, the data for indication on EIS come from the ADIRUs and the SDAC.

question: What is the result on the ECAM if an oxygen bottle squib has a loss of continuity?

options.a: A MASTER WARN and continuous chime
options.b: Single Chime, MASTER CAUT light, and an ECAM message
options.c: The SYS ON light turns red

justification: When a discontinuity occurs on the squib circuit, the following warnings are activated in the cockpit by the FWCs: Single Chime (SC), MASTER CAUT light, ECAM message.

question: What does a 'FAULT' operation signify when the cabin altitude is above 14,000 ft?

options.a: The masks have failed to drop
options.b: Relays 8WR and 9WR remain open after the 30-second delay
options.c: The oxygen pressure in the bottles is too low

justification: FAULT OPERATION: When the cabin altitude is more than 14,000 ft and relays 8WR and 9WR remain open after the delay of 30 seconds, a failure on the system occurs.

question: What condition must be met before the 'OXY/TMR RESET' P/BSW can be used to reset the system after operation?

options.a: The aircraft must be above 10,000 ft
options.b: The cabin altitude must be less than 10,000 ft
options.c: At least one engine must be stopped

justification: When the OXYGEN TMR RESET P/BSW is pushed and the cabin altitude is less than 10,000 ft, the oxygen regulators will close.

question: How long will the 'ON' light stay illuminated when the TMR RESET P/B is pushed to signal a successful reset?

options.b: 5 seconds
options.c: It stays on until takeoff

justification: When the TMR RESET P/BSW is pushed... the ON light comes on and stays on for 5 seconds.

question: What is the threshold for a 'low pressure' warning in the intermediate oxygen supply line?

options.a: 6.9 bar (100 psi) decreasing / 5.5 bar (80 psi) increasing
options.b: 4 psi above cabin pressure
options.c: 1500 psi absolute

justification: Intermediate Line Low Pressure Switch: The decreasing pressure is 6.9 bar (100 psi) and the increasing pressure is 5.5 ± 0.7 bar (80±10 psi).

question: In the event of a total loss of the oxygen pressure calculation, what is displayed on the POXIP?

options.c: FAIL

justification: A '- -' instead of a pressure value will be displayed on the POXIP and the respective fault indication on the front of QCCU comes on.

question: Where is the engine Overpressure Valve (OPV) located?

options.b: Downstream from the PRV (main bleed valve)
options.c: Between the IP and HP stages

justification: An Overpressure Valve (OPV) is installed downstream from the bleed valve to protect the system in case of overpressure.

question: Which component is an air-to-air heat exchanger used for bleed air temperature regulation?

options.b: The Precooler
options.c: The ASM

justification: The hot bleed air goes through an air-to-air heat exchanger called the precooler.

question: What is the function of the IP check valve?

options.a: To regulate pressure from the HP stage
options.b: To protect the IP stage from reverse flow when the HP valve is open
options.c: To bleed off excess pressure during takeoff

justification: The IP check valve protects the IP stage from reverse flow when the HP VLV is open.

question: Which sensor provides the temperature reading shown on the ECAM for the engine bleed system?

options.b: The heat exchanger outlet temperature sensor
options.c: The PRV inlet temperature sensor

justification: The heat exchanger outlet temperature sensor... reads the regulated temperature downstream from the precooler. This temperature is shown on the ECAM.

question: What provides the muscle power to open the Fan Air Valve (FAV)?

options.b: Pneumatic pressure from the fan discharge
options.c: Pneumatic pressure controlled by the FAV control thermostat

justification: The FAV is pneumatically controlled by an external servo-control: the FAV control thermostat (CTL THERMST).

question: Where is the PRV control solenoid located relative to the precooler?

options.b: Downstream
options.c: Inside the primary exchanger

justification: The bleed pressure regulated valve control solenoid (CTL SOL) is located downstream from the precooler.

question: How is the PRV forced to close when the engine FIRE pushbutton is released out?

options.a: By cutting off its pneumatic muscle supply
options.b: By energizing the control solenoid to close the PRV
options.c: By closing the IP check valve

justification: The electrical mode with PRV shut-off function through energization of the control solenoid is used when... the ENGine FIRE P/B is RELEASED OUT.

question: What pressure threshold activates the Overpressure Valve (OPV) to start closing?

options.b: 75 psi
options.c: 85 psi

justification: The Overpressure Valve (OPV)... starts to close at 75 psi.

question: What is the pneumatic regulation range of the High Pressure Valve (HPV)?

options.b: Between 8 and 36 psi
options.c: At a constant 44 psi

justification: The HP VLV pneumatically regulates the air supply between 8 and 36 psi.

question: Which pressure sensor is used to monitor the HP valve (HPV) and the PRV status for the BMC?

options.b: The transferred pressure transducer
options.c: The IP sensor

justification: A transducer... reads the transferred pressure downstream from the High Pressure Valve (HPV). This pressure is used to monitor the PRV and the HPV.

question: Which components give the actual temperature of the mixer unit to the ACSCs?

options.b: Two mixer unit temperature sensors
options.c: The cabin recirculation fans

justification: There are two mixer unit temperature sensors... They give the actual temperature of the mixer unit to the Air Conditioning System Controllers (ASCSs).

question: Which zone is normally supplied from Pack 1 via the mixer unit?

options.b: Cockpit
options.c: Aft cabin

justification: Normally, the mixer unit lets the cockpit be supplied from pack 1 and FWD and aft cabins from pack 2.

question: What happens if Pack 1 fails, according to the mixer unit flap operation?

options.a: The cockpit loses all fresh air supply
options.b: An electrically operated flap ensures sufficient fresh air is delivered to the cockpit
options.c: Pack 2 flow is restricted to the cabin only

justification: An electrically operated mixer unit flap is installed to ensure that sufficient fresh air is delivered to the cockpit in case of pack 1 failure.

question: How much cabin air is typically mixed with conditioned air from the packs in the mixer unit?

options.b: Varies from 37% to 51%
options.c: Always less than 20%

justification: The quantity of cabin air mixed with conditioned air varies from 37% to 51%.

question: Which unit is used to ventilate the cabin zone temperature sensors?

options.b: The lavatory and galley ventilation system fan
options.c: The pack turbine exhaust

justification: NOTE: The LAV and GALY ventilation system is also used to ventilate the cabin zone temperature sensors.

question: How many thermistors are included in each zone temperature sensor?

options.b: Two (one for ACSC 1 and one for ACSC 2)
options.c: Three (for triple redundancy)

justification: Each zone temperature sensor has two thermistors, one connected to ACSC 1 and the other to ACSC 2.

question: If an overheat (above 88°C) is detected in one of the three supply ducts, what is the system response?

options.a: The associated pack FCV is closed
options.b: The ACSCs close the trim air PRV and all Trim Air Valves (TAV) automatically
options.c: The cabin recirculation fans are accelerated

justification: In case of overheat... (temperature above 88°C or 190°F), the ACSCs close the trim air PRV and all Trim Air Valves (TAV) automatically.

question: Where is the cockpit mixer unit temperature sensor connected?

options.b: To ACSC 1 only
options.c: To ACSC 2 only

justification: The cockpit mixer unit temperature sensor is connected to the ACSC 1 and the cabin mixer unit to the ACSC 2.

question: Which unit calculates the necessary temperature regulation for the cockpit zone?

options.b: ACSC 2
options.c: The CIDS Director

justification: The trim air valves are operated by ACSC 1 for the cockpit and ACSC 2 for the FWD and aft cabin zones.

question: Which of the following is true regarding the cabin recirculation fans in normal operation?

options.a: They provide constant flow indications on the ECAM
options.b: There are no ECAM indications associated with the cabin fans in normal operation
options.c: They are automatically disabled during takeoff

justification: In normal operation, there are no ECAM indications associated with the cabin fans.

question: Which of the following is a potential ignition source for an oxygen-related fire?

options.b: Incandescent particles from grinding
options.c: Pure aluminum

justification: The ignition sources include Raw flame, Incandescent particles (from grinding), and Electrical overheating.

question: What is the result of oxygen reacting with steel over a long period?

options.b: Oxidation (rust)
options.c: Nitrogen creation
