justification: The reaction can be slow and can cause for example steel oxidation commonly called rust.

question: Why is pure oxygen at high pressure particularly dangerous when in contact with petroleum products?

options.a: It dilutes the fuel and causes engine failure
options.b: It will react violently and can cause fire or explosion
options.c: It turns the petroleum into a solid mass

justification: Pure oxygen at high pressure will react violently with materials such as oil, grease... and will get powerfully in fire.

question: What material should maintenance personnel use for cleaning the area around oxygen components?

options.b: Approved cleaner as defined in the AMM
options.c: Only water and a dry rag

justification: The area around the oxygen components must always be cleaned with approved cleaner before and after any work done on the system.

question: What should be done with oxygen units after they are removed from the aircraft?

options.b: Put into a sealed vinyl bag
options.c: Immediately discharged for safety

justification: Put dry, clean, metal or plastic plugs on all pipes or units removed temporarily. Put each pipe or unit in a sealed vinyl bag.

question: What is the risk if standard oil is used to lubricate a connector thread in the oxygen system?

options.a: The threads will seize over time
options.b: Risk of explosion upon contact with oxygen
options.c: The ECAM pressure readings will be inaccurate

justification: WARNING: NEVER USE STANDARD OIL TO LUBRICATE THE CONNECTOR THREAD (risk of explosion).

question: What should be used if a person catches fire in an oxygen-enriched atmosphere?

options.b: They must be sprayed with water and carried to free air immediately
options.c: A fire blanket only

justification: The victim must be sprayed of water and carried outside in free air as soon as possible.

question: Why is skin oil from bare hands considered a maintenance hazard in the oxygen system?

options.a: It makes the components slippery to handle
options.b: It is a source of contamination and can react with oxygen
options.c: It prevents the sensors from reading correctly

justification: Do not touch connection ends and interior of oxygen components with bare hands, because skin oil and bacteria are a source of contamination.

question: What tool safety measure is required during oxygen maintenance?

options.a: Tools must be heated before use
options.b: Tools must be clean and free of oil traces
options.c: Only magnetic tools are allowed

justification: Any tool, rag, cloth, or equipment that is not clean and free of oil traces must not be used.

question: What is the recommended personal protective equipment for handling oxygen components?

options.b: Clean cotton gloves
options.c: Rubber insulated gloves

justification: Always work with clean clothes and tools. Keep your hands clean (possibly, wear gloves in cotton).

question: Which areas are protected by potable and waste water line anti-ice?

options.a: Only the main external fill points
options.b: Potable and waste water lines in sections 13 and 14
options.c: The entire length of the waste water system from nose to tail

justification: The potable and waste water lines in sections 13 and 14 are insulated and electrically heated.

question: Where is the manual test pushbutton for the water line anti-ice system found?

options.b: Directly on the system control unit
options.c: In the aft galley

justification: A manual test of the system is available via a P/B located on the control unit.

question: What is the regulation temperature for the water lines anti-ice system?

options.b: Between 6°C (43°F) and 10°C (50°F)
options.c: At a constant 15°C

justification: The heating temperature (regulated by the control unit) is between 6°C (43°F) and 10°C (50°F).

question: How many sensors are associated with the water lines anti-ice control unit?

options.b: Two sensors
options.c: Four sensors (one for each heater)

justification: The system comprises a control unit and heater assemblies associated to two sensors.

question: Which power source supplies the water line anti-ice heating assemblies?

options.b: 115 VAC
options.c: 26 VAC

justification: The diagrams for water line anti-ice (e.g. page 402/403) show HEATING AC POWER (115 VAC) is supplied to the assemblies.

question: In the event of a control unit failure, what indications are given on the front of the unit itself?

options.b: Red 'FAULT' LEDs will illuminate
options.c: The 'OK' LEDs will go out (as shown in standard OK/Check logic)

justification: The diagrams and text show that 'OK' LEDs come on if the test is satisfactory; failure would be indicated by their absence during the test.

question: What occurs if the air stop drain valve heater reaches 120°C?

options.a: It switches to low power mode
options.b: The overheat protection activates
options.c: The valve automatically opens to vent heat

justification: The overheat protection (for air stop drain valve) is at 120°C (248°F).

question: Is the overflow nipple at the potable water service panel heated on the A320 model?

options.a: Yes, on all Single Aisle aircraft
options.b: No, it is only heated on the A318, A319, and A321
options.c: Only as a customer option

justification: NOTE: On the A318/A319/A321 the overflow nipple at the potable water service panel is also electrically heated. (Excluding A320).

question: What is the function of the 'HTR' and 'CU' lights on the Drain Mast Control Unit?

options.a: They remain on throughout the entire flight
options.b: They are ON as long as the TEST P/BSW is pressed to indicate correct operation
options.c: They only illuminate when a fault is detected

justification: On the front face of the CU, the HTR and CU lights are ON as long as the associated TEST P/BSW is pressed in.

question: Where are the failures for the Drain Mast system stored for retrieval by maintenance?

options.b: In the Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU)
options.c: On the FAP memory cassette

justification: The drain mast data is stored in the Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU).

question: Where is the HP ground connector located?

options.b: Under the belly fairing through a small access door
options.c: Near the APU exhaust

justification: Get access to the HP ground connector through a small access door which is on the lower fuselage belly fairing.

question: To which part of the pneumatic system does the HP ground connector provide air?

options.b: Only the LH bleed system
options.c: Directly to the engine starters only

justification: Only the LH bleed system is supplied (via the ground air cart).

question: How can the ground air supply be used to feed both the LH and RH systems?

options.b: By selecting the X BLEED valve selector to OPEN
options.c: By selecting the APU bleed to ON

justification: When the X BLEED valve selector is selected in the OPEN position, the ground air supply will be available to supply the LH and RH system together.

question: How is the crossbleed valve operated during a ground air start?

options.b: Manually by the crew
options.c: Pneumatically by the ground cart pressure

justification: During a ground air start, the crossbleed valve must be operated manually.

question: What allows the ground air to supply the right side pneumatic system?

options.a: The check valve in the APU duct
options.b: Opening the crossbleed valve
options.c: Closing both engine bleed valves

justification: The right side may be supplied by opening the crossbleed valve.

question: What is the recommended procedure for starting the second engine using ground air?

options.a: Start it directly with the ground air supply connected
options.b: Disconnect the ground air and perform a crossbleed start using the first engine
options.c: Leave the first engine off and use ground air for both separately

justification: For safety, it is recommended to use the ground air supply to start the first engine. Then disconnect... and perform a crossbleed start for the second engine.

question: Where does the crew see the evidence that ground air pressure is available?

options.a: The 'GND' light on the AIR COND panel
options.b: The left bleed system pressure indicator on the ECAM
options.c: A 'GND SPLY OK' message on the EWD

justification: The left bleed system pressure indicator will indicate pressure when the ground air is supplied.

question: Which side of the crossbleed duct is the ground air supply duct connected to?

options.b: The right hand side
options.c: The center intersection

justification: The ground air supply duct is connected to the left hand side of the crossbleed duct.

question: What is the purpose of selecting the X-BLEED to OPEN when using ground air for air conditioning?

options.a: To equalize the pressure between the two packs
options.b: To allow ground air to supply the RH side system
options.c: To prevent backflow into the APU

justification: When the X-BLEED selector is in the OPEN position, the ground air supply will be available to supply the LH and RH system together.

question: Does the 'GND' indication on ECAM depend on the ground air cart being connected?

options.b: No, it appears when the aircraft is on ground to show the supply location
options.c: Only if the crossbleed valve is closed

justification: The GND indication DOES NOT indicate ground air supply connected or available. This indication appears when the aircraft is on the ground.

question: What component is used for 'short term' and 'fast' pack discharge temperature response?

options.b: The Bypass Valve (BYP VLV)
options.c: The water extractor

justification: This temperature control (Bypass Valve) is used for short term and for a fast pack response.

question: Which sensor provides the primary feedback for pack outlet temperature regulation to the ACSC?

options.b: The WATER EXTRACTOR TEMP SENSOR
options.c: The RAM AIR temperature sensor

justification: The ACSC monitors the value from the WATER EXTRACTOR TEMP SENSOR to modulate the pack outlet temperature.

question: What is the simultaneous action of the Bypass Valve and Ram Air Inlet flap to increase cooling?

options.a: Ram air inlet flap closes more, bypass valve opens more
options.b: Ram air inlet flap opens more, bypass valve closes more
options.c: Both components close fully

justification: To increase cooling, the ram air inlet flap opens more and the BYP valve closes more.

question: Where does the air bypassed by the BYP VLV come from and go to?

options.a: From the pack inlet to the mixer unit
options.b: From the ACM compressor inlet to the turbine outlet
options.c: From the primary heat exchanger to the atmosphere

justification: When controlled to a more open position, the valve bypasses hot air from the ACM compressor inlet around the ACM to the turbine outlet.

question: Which sensor is used to monitor the position of the ram air inlet flap?

options.a: The SPEED AND DIRECTION SENSOR attached to the actuator
options.b: A linear potentiometer on the flap hinges
options.c: A digital encoder in the ACSC

justification: The position of the ram air inlet flap is monitored by the SPEED AND DIRECTION SENSOR attached to the actuator.

question: What is the function of the bypass valve when icing is detected at the condenser?

options.a: It closes fully to force all air through the turbine
options.b: It opens more to let hot air flow directly into the turbine outlet to melt the ice
options.c: It cycles open/closed every 5 seconds

justification: This causes the ACSC to command the bypass valve (BYP VLV) to a more open position and hot air flows directly into the turbine outlet airflow. This hot air will melt the ice.

question: What happens if there is no positive effect on compressor outlet temperature after the ram air flap opens fully?

options.b: The ACSC sends a signal to the torque motor of the FCV to control it to a more closed position
options.c: The opposite pack switches to high flow

justification: If there is no positive effect... the ACSC will send a signal to the torque motor of the FCV to control it to a more closed position. This will decrease the hot air supply.

question: Why is the ram air inlet flap controlled to the fully closed position during takeoff and landing?

options.b: To prevent dirt ingestion from the nose landing gear
options.c: To increase the cabin pressure rate of change

justification: In some special aircraft configurations (take-off and landing), the ram air flap is controlled to the fully closed position to prevent dirt ingestion from the nose landing gear.

question: What is the normal operating limit for compressor discharge temperature monitored by the ACSC?

options.c: Up to 260°C

justification: Pack temperature control: up to 180°C (385°F): normal operation.

question: At what compressor discharge temperature does the ram air inlet flap start to open more to increase airflow?

options.b: Between 180°C and 220°C
options.c: Exactly 260°C

justification: 180°C to 220°C (428°F): the ram air inlet flap opens more in order to increase the RAM airflow.

question: Where is the automatically discharged fire bottle for a lavatory waste bin located?

options.b: Above the waste bin in each lavatory
options.c: In the main landing gear bay

justification: The protection of each lavatory waste bin is done by an automatic fire extinguishing system... The bottle is located above the waste bin.

question: How is the lavatory fire bottle discharged during a fire?

options.a: By an electrical signal from the cockpit
options.b: Automatically when a fusible material in the discharge tube melts
options.c: When the smoke detector reaches 10% obscuration

justification: The fusible material in the discharge tube melts at high temperature and the pressurized agent is discharged.

question: How can the pressure of a lavatory fire bottle be verified by maintenance?

options.b: By checking the pressure gage on the bottle
options.c: Using a special test tool connected to the CIDS

justification: The lavatory fire bottle pressure may be checked at the pressure gage on the bottle.

question: What cockpit warning is generated when smoke is detected in a lavatory?

options.a: A red MASTER WARN light and the LAVATORY SMOKE message on EWD
options.b: Only a Single Chime
options.c: The SMOKE light on the CARGO SMOKE panel

justification: SDF 1 or 2 sends a smoke alert... which generates the following cockpit warnings: a Continuous Repetitive Chime (CRC), the red MASTER WARNing light, the LAVATORY SMOKE warning message on the EWD.

question: Which cabin indication alerts the flight attendants to smoke in a specific lavatory?

options.a: A steady amber light on the ACP
options.b: A flashing amber light on the ACP and a 'SMOKE LAV X' message on the AIPs
options.c: The oxygen masks drop in that lavatory

justification: When smoke is detected... a flashing amber light on the related Area Call Panel (ACP), 'SMOKE LAV X' message is displayed and a red indicator flashes on all the Attendant Indication Panels (AIPs).

question: If a lavatory smoke detector fails, what is the dispatch requirement per the MEL?

options.a: The aircraft is limited to daylight flights only
options.b: The aircraft may be dispatched with the lavatory locked closed and the waste bin empty
options.c: The detector must be replaced before the next flight

justification: If this detector fails, the aircraft may be dispatched with the lavatory locked closed and the waste bin empty.

question: How is a lavatory locked closed for dispatch in the event of a detector failure?

options.a: Using a standard padlock through the door handle
options.b: Lift the 'LAVATORY' cover plate on the outside and slide the unlocking pin to the LOCK position
options.c: Secure the door with safety tape

justification: To lock the lavatory, lift the 'LAVATORY' cover plate on the outside of the door and slide the unlocking pin to the LOCK position.

question: What is the function of the Smoke Detection page on the FAP during a lavatory smoke alert?

options.a: It allows the crew to discharge the lavatory fire bottle
options.b: It appears automatically, displaying a red message and an icon of the affected location
options.c: It lists the remaining battery life of the smoke detector

justification: SMOKE DETECTION page appears automatically... on which 'SMOKE DETECTED' red message is displayed and a red icon is displayed at the affected location.

question: In the event of a lavatory detection fault, what color icon is displayed on the FAP SMOKE DETECTION page?

options.b: Amber
options.c: Yellow

justification: The lavatory detection fault is shown... an amber icon displayed at the affected location on the SMOKE DETECTION page.

question: Which system component automatically isolates a faulty lavatory smoke detector in the bus system?

options.b: The CIDS-SDF
options.c: The SDAC

justification: When a lavatory smoke detector failure is detected by CIDS-SDF, the faulty detector is automatically isolated in the bus system.

question: What allows the filling of the oxygen cylinder without its removal from the aircraft?

options.b: The optional filling connector on the oxygen fill panel
options.c: Connecting to the engine HP bleed port

justification: The optional filling connector makes it possible to fill the oxygen cylinder without removal of the cylinder from the aircraft.

question: Which bus supplies power to the CREW OXY SPLY system?

options.b: 28V DC ESS BUS (via 401PP)
options.c: 115V AC BUS 1

justification: The diagram on page 489/490 shows 28V DC ESS BUS (401PP) supplying the system.

question: What must be calculated before replenishing oxygen cylinders on the ground?

options.b: The average pressure in the replenished cylinders using aircraft placards
options.c: The exact number of masks expected for the next flight

justification: To check the correct fill pressure, you have to calculate the average pressure in the replenished oxygen cylinders... determined by the use of the aircraft placards.

question: What is the purpose of the reflective yellow area shown on the discharge indicator?

options.a: To indicate the system is currently being filled
options.b: To show that the cylinder has discharged or the relief valve is open
options.c: To indicate low cylinder temperature

justification: In case of overpressure... the green burst disk is blown out and a reflective yellow area of the discharge indicator is shown.

question: Where is the oxygen temperature transducer located?

options.b: In the installation area of oxygen cylinders
options.c: Inside the high-pressure filling line

justification: The temperature transducer measures the ambient temperature in the installation area of oxygen cylinders.

question: Which specialized tool is used to detect leaks during the oxygen servicing panel test?

options.b: A Helium detector (with helium as a tracer gas)
options.c: A standard soap and water bubble solution

justification: The diagram on page 473 shows a 'HELIUM DETECTOR' and 'HELIUM IS AN ASPHYXIATING GAS' warning during leak detection.

question: What is the threshold for the ECAM oxygen pressure indication to flash in green for a 77 cuft bottle?

options.b: Less than 800 psig
options.c: Less than 1500 psig

justification: The indication flashes in green when the pressure is less than 800 psig and the DOOR/OXY page comes into view automatically (for a 77 cuft bottle).

question: At what pressure does the burst disc of the oxygen cylinder rupture at 71°C?

options.b: 2451 psig (169 bar)
options.c: 2770 psig

justification: The burst disc will rupture at a pressure of 169 bar (2451 psig) at a temperature of 71°C (160°F).

question: Which of the following is an 'approved method' for checking oxygen system leaks mentioned in the diagrams?

options.b: Sherlock Type I or Snoop leak detection products
options.c: Petroleum-based grease

justification: The diagram on page 473 shows 'SHERLOCK' and 'Snoop' as approved LEAK DETECTION PRODUCTS.

question: During the 'Close-up' of a crew oxygen cylinder installation, what must be done to the circuit breaker?

options.a: Open and tag it for flight
options.b: Remove the safety clip and tag, then close the circuit breaker
options.c: The C/B must remain open for 24 hours

justification: Close-up: Remove the safety clip and the tag and close the circuit breaker.

question: What is the priority source for pneumatic air when both thrust levers are in the IDLE position?

options.b: The HP stage (via High Pressure Valves)
options.c: The APU

justification: With both thrust levers in the idle position, the HP (High Pressure) Valves (VLVs) are open and supplying air.

question: Which stage supplies bleed air when engine power is increased to the Takeoff (TO) position?

options.b: The Intermediate Pressure (IP) stage
options.c: Fan discharge air

justification: When the power... is increased to the Takeoff (TO) position, the HP VLV is closed, and the bleed air is supplied by the Intermediate Pressure (IP) stage.

question: Why does the High Pressure Valve (HPV) close when engine power increases?

options.a: To prevent damage to the air conditioning packs from excessive pressure
options.b: Because IP stage pressure becomes sufficient and switching is done pneumatically
options.c: To save fuel at high power settings

justification: Switching between IP and HP is done pneumatically... Once the IP bleed is sufficient, the HPV closes.

question: What is the status of the PRV, FAV, and HPV when the engines are shut down?

options.a: They remain in their last position
options.b: They are springloaded closed due to the lack of air pressure
options.c: They are locked in the OPEN position for ground maintenance

justification: When the engines are shut down, the PRV, Fan Air Valve (FAV) and HP VLV are springloaded closed due to the lack of air pressure.

question: Which unit provides the N2 signal used by the BMC to monitor engine status?

options.b: The Engine Interface Unit (EIU)
options.c: The ADIRU

justification: The BMCs receive signals... from the corresponding Engine Interface Unit (EIU). The diagram on page 37 shows EIU providing Engine Start/N2 parameters.

question: What pressure threshold (PS3) is required for the BMC to automatically energize the solenoid to maintain the HP valve closed on CFM56 engines?

options.b: 80 psi
options.c: 110 psi

justification: The solenoid will be energized by the BMC when... the pressure PS3 is greater than... 80 psi for the CFM-56 engines.

question: At what altitude is the High Pressure Valve (HPV) maintained closed by the BMC in flight for A318/319 models?

options.b: Above 15,000 ft
options.c: Always when in 'flight' status regardless of altitude

justification: The solenoid will be energized by the BMC when... the altitude is over 15,000 ft.

question: What is the regulated temperature that the Fan Air Valve (FAV) maintains at the precooler outlet?
justification: The Fan Air Valve (FAV) pneumatically regulates the fan airflow to the precooler for bleed air temperature regulation at 200°C (392°F).

question: Which ARINC 429 input to the BMC provides the flight phase data?

options.b: Centralized Fault Display Interface Unit (CFDIU)
options.c: EIU

justification: The diagram on page 37 shows digital inputs from CFDIU providing 'GMT, DATE, FLIGHT PHASE'.

question: How is the Pressure Regulating Valve (PRV) forced to close when reverse flow is detected?

options.a: By an electrical signal from the opposite BMC
options.b: Pneumatically when a delta pressure between precooler outlet and PRV inlet is detected
options.c: By mechanical linkage from the IP check valve

justification: The pneumatic mode is used for: reverse flow protection - the PRV is closed when a delta pressure between the precooler outlet and the PRV inlet is detected.

question: What determines if an oxygen container door is spring-loaded or not?

options.b: The container type (Type II is spring-loaded, Type I is not)
options.c: Whether gaseous or chemical oxygen is used

justification: A container door (spring loaded for type II, type I not spring loaded).

question: Where are 'Type II' oxygen containers typically installed?

options.b: In sidewalls, ceilings, lavatories and galleys
options.c: Only in the cockpit

justification: Type II installed in sidewalls, ceilings, lavatories and galleys to supply 2 persons with oxygen.

question: What component in the container activates the flow to an individual mask?

options.b: A lanyard pulled by the passenger
options.c: A remote-controlled solenoid

justification: For each mask, there is... a SOV activated automatically by a lanyard.

question: How is the oxygen container door latched in a gaseous oxygen system?

options.b: Pneumatically
options.c: With an electrical solenoid only

justification: The oxygen masks container doors open pneumatically (in gaseous systems).

question: What pressure range is required to actuate the door latches in an ETOPS gaseous oxygen system?

options.b: 1.5 bar to 3.0 bar
options.c: 1850 psi

justification: When the door latch actuation pressure (1.5 bar - 3.0 bar) is reached, the doors of the oxygen container assemblies... will be released.

question: What happens if a Main Distribution Line (MDL) is damaged due to an engine burst?

options.a: The entire oxygen system is vented overboard
options.b: The SOV and check valve on the damaged part close to seal the area
options.c: The oxygen cylinders are automatically jettisoned

justification: In case of damage... the surge flow... will induce the SOV... to close. The reverse flow check valve... will also close in order to seal the damaged area.

question: In the event of a damaged riser line, will the masks associated with that line still deploy?

options.b: No, the doors of the oxygen containers in the damaged RL will not be released
options.c: Only if manually opened by the crew

justification: The doors of the oxygen container will be released (except the doors of the oxygen containers in the damaged RL).

question: How many persons can be supplied by a 'Type I' oxygen container?

options.b: 2 to 4 persons
options.c: Only 2 persons

justification: Type I installed in the overhead stowage PSU channels to supply 2 to 4 persons.

question: What provides the backup to the CIDS-SDF if one director fails?

options.b: The remaining SDF card in the other CIDS director
options.c: The ACSC takes over the logic

justification: If one SDF card in one CIDS director fails, the smoke detection function is transferred to the remaining SDF card in the other CIDS director.

question: Which bus provides the 115 VAC power to the electrical latch assemblies in the standard passenger oxygen system?

options.b: AC ESS BUS (via 801XP)
options.c: AC BUS 2

justification: The busbar 801XP supplies 115 VAC to the electrical latch assemblies of the emergency oxygen containers.
